mission.name: What's in a Name
mission.description: 80 chunks were carved out of the crashed upload volume into recovered/. The carver guessed their extensions, mostly wrong, and some chunks have none (RECOVERY-NOTES.txt). The upload service needs them sorted by what they really are.
mission.objective: Move every chunk from recovered/ to sorted/<type>/chunk-NNN.<type>, where <type> is its real content: gz, bz2, xz, zip, tar, tar.gz (a gzip that holds a tar archive), png, pdf or txt. Zero-byte chunks go to sorted/empty/chunk-NNN with no extension. Keep the content unchanged and leave nothing in recovered/.

mission.name: Time and Permission
mission.description: The acme-agent installer refuses the extracted bundle: the vendor's MANIFEST pins the mode and mtime of every path, and some entries drifted during extraction (INSTALLER-ERROR.txt). Several names contain spaces, and lib/ holds a symlink.
mission.objective: First write drift.txt in the sandbox root: one line per MANIFEST path whose mode or mtime differs, written exactly as in MANIFEST. Then fix the bundle so every entry (the symlink itself included) has exactly the mode and mtime MANIFEST gives, without changing anything else.

mission.name: Dead Weight
mission.description: projects/ is going to cold storage, and the archive should not carry caches that any build can recreate (ARCHIVE-PLAN.txt). First the team wants to see which cache dirs are worth excluding.
mission.objective: Write bloat.txt in the sandbox root: one line 'KiB<TAB>path' for every directory named node_modules, .cache, target or build under projects/ that uses more than 5 MiB (5120 KiB) on disk, sorted largest first. Size = what `du -sk` reports for that dir, path relative like projects/app/build. Only the outermost cache dir counts: skip cache dirs that sit inside another cache dir. Don't delete anything.

mission.name: Will It Fit
mission.description: The catalog restore.tar.xz has to be unpacked into /srv on every kiosk that can take it (RESTORE-TICKET.txt). You can't log in to the kiosks; all you have is last night's df -PT and df -i output of each one in hosts/.
mission.objective: Write targets.txt with the names of the hosts (file names in hosts/ without .txt, one per line) that can take the restore: the filesystem that holds /srv on that host must have at least as many free KiB as the uncompressed size of restore.tar.xz (the tar inside, in KiB rounded up) and at least as many free inodes as the archive has members (files and directories).

mission.name: Needle in a Gzip Stack
mission.description: Support needs the full history of order 88412 (TICKET.txt). Its log lines are spread over two weeks of rotated logs in logs/: app.log, app.log.1, then compressed rotations, some gzip, some bzip2, some xz. The disk is almost full, so nothing gets unpacked.
mission.objective: Write order-88412.txt with every log line whose order= field is exactly 88412, from all files in logs/, oldest first, as plain log lines (no file names in front). Leave every file in logs/ as it is and don't write decompressed copies anywhere.

mission.name: Pack Light
mission.description: orders-api 2.4.0 is ready to ship. The release tarball is built from the working copy in app/, which also holds a git repo, node_modules, log files and production secrets (RELEASE-CHECKLIST.txt).
mission.objective: Create release.tar.gz in the sandbox root, gzip-compressed, with members starting with app/. It must contain every file of app/ except: the .git directory and .gitignore, every node_modules directory (at any depth), every *.log file, and every file named exactly .env. .env.example files, logs/.keep and .github/ must be included. Don't change app/.

mission.name: Week of Incrementals
mission.description: Capstone. data/ gets a full backup on Sunday and incremental backups Monday to Wednesday (BACKUP-PLAN.txt). It is Sunday evening; ./simulate-day.sh plays each next day, and on Thursday the data disk dies. Needs GNU tar (Linux).
mission.objective: Take backups/data-sun.tar.gz (full) now, then after each of ./simulate-day.sh mon, tue and wed take backups/data-mon.tar.gz, data-tue.tar.gz and data-wed.tar.gz: gzip-compressed GNU incremental archives that hold only what changed. Then run ./simulate-day.sh thu and restore Wednesday's state into restored/, so that restored/data is exactly data/ as it was on Wednesday night, with files deleted during the week absent.

mission.name: Five Generations
mission.description: Capstone. Cron should run ./rotate.sh every night to keep five generations of the bakery's site backup (ROTATION.txt). Kim's draft of rotate.sh was never tested, and someone already deleted backups/site.tar.gz.3 by hand.
mission.objective: Make rotate.sh (executable, run from the sandbox root) keep backups/site.tar.gz.1 (newest) ... .5 (oldest): each run drops .5, moves every existing generation up by one (a missing one leaves its gap moving up too) and creates a fresh .1, a gzip tar of site/. It must exit 0, also when generations are missing, and leave nothing else in backups/. The check runs a copy of your script many times in a scratch folder.

mission.name: Trust, but Verify
mission.description: Capstone. A vendor's delivery/ holds eight archives and a SHA256SUMS file. Some names lie about the format, and the security team warns that at least one archive was tampered with and that archives can try to write outside the folder they are unpacked in (INTAKE-POLICY.txt).
mission.objective: Write audit.csv: the header name,real_type,members,checksum_ok,unsafe, then one row per archive with its file name, its real format (tar, tar.gz, tar.bz2, tar.xz or zip), the number of entries it lists (directories included), yes/no for matching SHA256SUMS, and yes/no for having a member path that is absolute or contains a .. component. Then extract every archive that matches its checksum and is safe into accepted/<name>/ (name = file name up to the first dot), and nothing else. No file may be written outside its accepted/ folder.

mission.name: Invoices for Legal
mission.description: Legal is preparing for an audit and wants a copy of every invoice PDF on the old shared drive. The dump in share/ grew for ten years without rules: Invoice_2026-03.PDF sits next to 'invoice - april.pdf', and templates, backups and receipts are mixed in.
mission.objective: Write the path of every file under share/ whose name contains the word invoice and ends in .pdf, both in any letter case, to invoices.txt (one path per line, like share/Finance/x.pdf or ./share/Finance/x.pdf). Nothing else goes in the list; do not change share/.

mission.name: After the Failed Deploy
mission.description: Last night's deploy died halfway through. Before anyone cleans up releases/, the on-call engineer wants two lists for the incident ticket: every symbolic link under releases/ (some point at shared folders, one may point at nothing) and every directory the deploy left completely empty.
mission.objective: Write links.txt with the path of every symbolic link under releases/, and empty-dirs.txt with the path of every empty directory under releases/ (one path per line, like releases/x or ./releases/x). A directory that holds anything, even a hidden file, is not empty. Do not change releases/.

mission.name: Too Big to Send
mission.description: The mail relay rejects every attachment larger than 10 MiB (10 x 1024 x 1024 bytes), and a crashed upload left zero-byte attachments behind. Messages in outbox/ keep bouncing, and support wants to tell each sender which file to fix.
mission.objective: Write oversize.txt with the path of every file under outbox/ that is larger than 10 MiB, and empty.txt with the path of every file under outbox/ that is 0 bytes (one path per line, like outbox/x or ./outbox/x). Files of exactly 10 MiB are still allowed. Do not change outbox/.

mission.name: What Changed Last Night
mission.description: The shop went down an hour ago and the first question in the incident channel is the usual one: which configs were touched recently? etc/ is a copy of the server's /etc with the original timestamps.
mission.objective: Write recent.txt with the path of every file under etc/ whose content was modified during the last 24 hours (one path per line, like etc/x or ./etc/x). Only files, not directories. Do not change anything in etc/.

mission.name: Compress the Old Logs
mission.description: app/logs fills the disk every few weeks because nobody configured rotation. Until logrotate is set up, ops wants the old logs compressed in place, with a single find command that can later go into cron.
mission.objective: Compress (gzip, in place, so x.log becomes x.log.gz with the same content) every file under app/logs whose name ends in .log and that was last modified more than 7 days ago. Logs modified within the last 7 days stay as they are, and no other file is compressed or changed.

mission.name: Leaked Keys
mission.description: Security found a paste with 40 of our API keys and saved them in leaked.txt, one per line. Before rotating them, they need to know which requests in logs/ were made with any of those keys. The keys contain characters like . + * and $.
mission.objective: Write hits.txt with every log line under logs/ that contains any of the keys from leaked.txt exactly as written, each prefixed with its file name the way grep prints it with several files (logs/dir/file.log:the whole line). No line numbers, no other lines. Do not change logs/.

mission.name: Root Over SSH
mission.description: An auditor asks which of our 12 servers let root log in over SSH with a password. Copies of their sshd configs are in hosts/<host>/sshd_config, edited by hand for years: commented-out lines, tabs, odd capitalisation, and settings that appear twice.
mission.objective: Write root-login-hosts.txt with the names of the hosts (the folder names under hosts/, one per line, any order) where sshd's effective PermitRootLogin setting is yes. Values like prohibit-password, without-password, forced-commands-only and no do not allow password logins, and a host without the setting uses the default, prohibit-password.

mission.name: What Is Actually Set
mission.description: A database is slow and the vendor asks for 'your effective postgresql.conf, without the comments'. Ours is the stock file of about 600 lines, edited over the years: commented defaults, indented comment lines, blank lines with stray spaces and tabs, and a few dozen real settings, some with a comment after the value.
mission.objective: Create effective.conf containing exactly the lines of postgresql.conf that are settings: drop every line that is empty, contains only spaces/tabs, or whose first non-blank character is #. Keep the remaining lines unchanged (including any # comment after a value) and in their original order. postgresql.conf itself must stay unchanged.

mission.name: The Noisiest Services
mission.description: Error budgets are reviewed tomorrow. logs/ holds today's log of each of our 30 services (logs/<service>.log, one line per event, the level in the second column). The SRE lead wants the services that logged more than 50 ERROR lines today.
mission.objective: Write noisy.txt with one line '<file> <count>' (for example 'billing.log 73') for every log in logs/ that has more than 50 lines with the level ERROR, sorted by count, highest first. Other levels never count, even when their message mentions something like NOERROR.

mission.name: Who Killed the Worker
mission.description: The image worker crashed 15 times overnight. A FATAL line never names the request it was working on, but the line just before each crash always carries that request's req=<id>. The developers want the ids so they can replay those requests.
mission.objective: Write fatal-reqs.txt with the request id (only the id, without req=) from the line directly before each FATAL in worker.log, one per line, in the order they occur in the log. When several FATAL lines follow each other, they belong to the request on the line before the first of them, which is listed once. Do not change worker.log.

mission.name: Columns for Two Audiences
mission.description: The asset database exported assets.tsv: tab-separated, a header line, 14 columns, and some values (models, rooms, notes) contain spaces. Ops wants a short list for the rack audit, and the hardware vendor needs the full export without our staff's e-mail addresses.
mission.objective: Create inventory.tsv with the columns serial, hostname, rack in exactly that order, and vendor.tsv with all columns of assets.tsv except owner_email, in their original order. Both keep the header line, every row of assets.tsv, and tabs between the fields. assets.tsv must stay unchanged.

mission.name: Three Exports, One Report
mission.description: The monitoring tool can only export one metric per file: hosts.txt, cpu.txt and mem.txt, one value per line, all in the same host order. cpu.txt came from the Windows reporting box. The team wants a single table, and the CPU-saturated hosts as a list for `ansible --limit`.
mission.objective: Create report.tsv with one line per host: host, cpu, mem separated by tabs, in the order of hosts.txt, no header. Create limit.txt with one single line: the hosts whose cpu is 90 or more, joined with commas (web-03,db-01,...), in report order, without spaces or a trailing comma. Leave the three input files unchanged.

mission.name: Whose Laptop Is That?
mission.description: The office network has devices nobody recognises. The DHCP server's lease file dnsmasq.leases (expiry mac ip hostname client-id) says which MAC got which IP; the asset inventory inventory.csv (MAC,owner,team, with a header) says who owns which MAC. The two systems write MAC addresses differently.
mission.objective: Write owners.txt with one line 'ip mac owner' for every lease in dnsmasq.leases: the MAC as the lease file writes it, the owner from inventory.csv, or UNKNOWN when the inventory has no entry for that MAC. Sort the lines by IP address numerically (10.20.0.9 before 10.20.0.10).

mission.name: Twin Servers Drift
mission.description: web-1 and web-2 sit behind the same load balancer and should be identical, but a deploy works on one and fails on the other. You have both package lists as dumped by the inventory agent: web1.pkgs and web2.pkgs (package<TAB>version, in install order). The two dumps were taken with different formats: web-1 adds the architecture to some names (libc6:amd64), web-2 never does.
mission.objective: Write only-web1.txt with the names of the packages installed on web-1 but not on web-2, and only-web2.txt with those installed on web-2 but not on web-1. One package name per line, each name once, without architecture or version. A package installed on both hosts in different versions is not drift.

mission.name: Capacity Review
mission.description: For the quarterly capacity review, the team wants the host inventory grouped by datacenter, busiest hosts first. inventory.txt (host dc rack load mem, with a header line) comes from a metrics exporter that writes some loads in scientific notation, like 1e-02 or 1.2e+01.
mission.objective: Write sorted.txt: the header line first, then every row of inventory.txt unchanged, ordered by datacenter (alphabetically), then by load as a number (highest first), then by host name in natural order (web9 before web10).
concepts: keeping a header out of sort

mission.name: Is It Beaconing?
mission.description: A laptop was quarantined after an antivirus alert. Malware often phones home by looking up the same odd domain again and again. You have two hours of the laptop's local DNS cache log, dnsmasq.log: every lookup is a query[...] line, followed by forwarded/reply or cached lines for the same name. Applications write names in any case, and some add a trailing dot (example.com.).
mission.objective: Count the query[...] lines per domain, treating names case-insensitively and ignoring a trailing dot. Write beacons.txt with one line 'count domain' for every domain queried 3 times or more, highest count first, and once.txt with every domain queried exactly once, one per line. Write domains in lowercase without the trailing dot.

mission.name: Usernames From HR
mission.description: 64 people start next month and HR sent their names in newhires.txt, exported from a Windows tool. Accounts are created from a list of usernames, and the naming rule is: all lowercase, name parts joined by an underscore (Mary J. Smith becomes mary_j_smith). The export separates name parts with spaces, double spaces or tabs, initials have dots, and some names are in capitals.
mission.objective: Write usernames.txt with one username per line, in the same order as newhires.txt: the name in lowercase, with every space, tab and dot turned into an underscore and runs of underscores squeezed into one. No carriage returns (\r) may remain.

mission.name: Serial Console Cleanup
mission.description: A database server failed to mount its backup share after a reboot. The datacenter tech captured the serial console (boot messages and a short login session) in console.raw for the incident ticket, but the capture is full of carriage returns, NUL padding bytes, terminal bells and ANSI colour codes, and the ticket system shows it as garbage.
mission.objective: Write console.txt: the text of console.raw, line by line, with every carriage return (\r), NUL byte, bell character (\a) and ANSI colour sequence (ESC [ ... m) removed. Everything else stays exactly as it is, including the tabs in the /etc/hosts lines and the empty lines.

mission.name: Vendor Ticket
mission.description: The vendor of the orders API asks for two things for their support ticket: the database settings from app.ini and the part of trace.log their crash tool pointed at, lines 1200 to 1260. app.ini has several sections, including a [database-replica] section that is not the one they want.
mission.objective: Write db-section.txt with the [database] section of app.ini: from its [database] header line up to, but not including, the next section header, every line unchanged. Write excerpt.txt with lines 1200 to 1260 of trace.log (both included), unchanged.

mission.name: CDN Cutover
mission.description: Marketing moves its static files to a new CDN tonight and wants ISO dates on the site at the same time. The 40 HTML templates in templates/ (and templates/emails/) still load everything from http://old-cdn.example.com/ and print dates as DD/MM/YYYY. Some templates also link to our print partner, whose domain is old-cdn-example.com; those links must stay.
mission.objective: Edit the templates in place: every http://old-cdn.example.com/<path> becomes https://cdn.example.net/v2/<path>, and every date written DD/MM/YYYY becomes YYYY-MM-DD. Nothing else may change (old-cdn-example.com links included), and no backup files may be left in templates/.

mission.name: Who Is Eating The Web Server?
mission.description: The shop's web server swapped all night and the load average stays high even though traffic is low. Before rebooting, the on-call engineer saved a snapshot of `ps aux` in ps-aux.txt (about 900 processes). Two questions: which web workers (user www-data) use too much memory, and which processes are stuck (state D, uninterruptible I/O) or dead but not reaped (state Z, zombie)?
mission.objective: Write heavy.txt with one line 'PID COMMAND' for every process of user www-data whose %MEM is more than 5, and stuck.txt with one line 'PID COMMAND' for every process whose state (STAT) is D or Z, whatever flags follow the letter. COMMAND is the complete command line with all its arguments. Keep the order of ps-aux.txt.

mission.name: Logfmt To CSV
mission.description: The new tracing dashboard imports CSV, but the shop's services log in logfmt: app.log has lines of key=value pairs such as ts=... level=info svc=api msg="request done" dur=850ms, with the keys in any order. Durations are written in microseconds (us), milliseconds (ms) or seconds (s), and some lines have no dur at all.
mission.objective: Write slow.csv: the header line ts,svc,dur_ms, then one line ts,svc,dur_ms for every log line whose dur= value is more than 500 milliseconds, in the order of app.log. ts and svc are copied from the ts= and svc= keys; dur_ms is the duration in milliseconds as a whole number, rounded (1.2s becomes 1200). Other keys that merely contain those names (db_dur, upstream_svc) are not the ones you want.

mission.name: NAS Storage Bill
mission.description: The NAS is 92% full and management wants to charge storage back to its users. Someone already ran find /nas -printf '%p\t%u\t%s\t%TY-%Tm-%Td\n' > files.lst 2>&1, so files.lst has one line per file: path, owner, size in bytes and last-modified date, separated by tabs. Paths contain spaces, a few files are tens of GiB, and the find errors went into the file too.
mission.objective: Write usage.txt with one line per user: the user name, the total size of their files in GiB (1 GiB = 1024^3 bytes), and the size of their files last modified before 2025-01-01 in GiB, separated by tabs, both numbers with exactly two decimals (e.g. amira<TAB>812.34<TAB>401.20). Sort the lines by total GiB, largest first.

mission.name: Weekly Bounce Report
mission.description: Every Monday the mail team asks which customers' mailings bounce the most, so they can warn them before the relays land on a blocklist. The logs of both relays are under var/log/ (rotated daily, older ones gzipped). Postfix writes the sender of a message (from=) and its delivery result (status=) on different lines, linked by the queue ID. Some bounces come from the empty sender <> (bounce notices that bounced themselves).
mission.objective: From every mail.log* file under var/log/ (any depth, plain or .gz) modified in the last 7 days, count the bounced messages (status=bounced) per sender domain: the part after @ in the message's from=<...>, in lowercase; messages from the empty sender <> don't count. Write report.txt with the top 5 as lines 'rank domain count' (e.g. '1 example.org 17'): highest count first, equal counts ordered by domain name. Don't change or unpack the logs.
concepts: awk arrays as a join on a key

mission.name: Who Logs In?
mission.description: A ticket from the security team: "Who can actually log in to web-03?" You have copies of the server's etc/passwd and etc/shells.
mission.objective: Write humans.txt with the login names (one per line, any order) of every account on web-03 that a person can open a shell with: a UID in the regular user range 1000-59999 and a login shell listed in etc/shells. Also list any account other than root itself that has UID 0, because it is root under another name. Leave etc/passwd and etc/shells unchanged.

mission.name: Docker Crew
mission.description: Membership of the docker group is root-equivalent, so the auditors want to know who on build-02 has it. You have copies of the server's etc/group and etc/passwd.
mission.objective: Write docker-members.txt with every user who is in the docker group on build-02, one login name per line, in any order. A user is in a group when it is listed as a member on that group's line, or when it is the user's primary group. Leave etc/group and etc/passwd unchanged.

mission.name: Permission Denied on One Host
mission.description: The release job fails with "permission denied" writing to /var/www on some of the five web and API hosts, though it works on the others. The output of `id deploy` was captured on each host into id-<host>.txt.
mission.objective: Write missing.txt with the names of the hosts (web-01, api-02, ...; one per line, any order) where deploy is not in the www-data group in any way. Then, for the ticket, write me.txt with your own UID and primary GID as two numbers on one line, like "1000 1000", taken from your real account.

mission.name: Fake It
mission.description: deploy.sh should only run for the account named in deploy.allowed, but the security review (NOTE.txt) shows that `USER=release ./deploy.sh` gets anyone through, because the guard compares the name with $USER.
mission.objective: Change the guard in deploy.sh so it compares deploy.allowed with the user the script is really running as. A caller whose real account is not the allowed one must be refused with exit status 1, even with USER or LOGNAME faked; the allowed account must be able to deploy whatever USER says and also when USER and LOGNAME are not set at all (as under cron). Keep reading the allowed name from deploy.allowed and keep the rest of the script working.

mission.name: Stale Sessions
mission.description: Kim was added to the docker group an hour ago but still gets "permission denied" on the socket. Group changes only reach a process at login, so anyone who was already logged in when their groups changed has the same problem. The Uid/Gid/Groups lines of every running session were captured into sessions/<user>.status.
mission.objective: Write relogin.txt with the login names (one per line, any order) of every user whose running session is missing a group (their primary group included) that etc/group and etc/passwd give them now. These users must log in again. A user whose session holds a group they no longer have is not on this list. The session files show numbers only; bin/id, bin/groups and bin/getent read the group database like the real tools. Leave the captured files unchanged.
concepts: group changes need a new login

mission.name: Which ID Comes Next?
mission.description: Tomorrow you create two accounts on app-04: `metrics`, a system account for the exporter (useradd -r), and `lena`, a new colleague (a normal user with her own private group). Change control wants the exact IDs written on the ticket before anything is created.
mission.objective: Work out, from etc/login.defs, etc/passwd and etc/group, the UID and GID that useradd would give each new account, and write next-ids.txt with two lines: `lena UID GID` and `metrics UID GID`. Each account gets a private group named after it. Do not create the accounts and leave the three files unchanged.

mission.name: Who Is Root on db-01?
mission.description: Audit finding: nobody can say who gets full root on db-01. You have a copy of its etc/sudoers, the drop-in files in etc/sudoers.d/ and etc/group. Everyone with a username, an alias or a group in a rule counts, but only if sudo would really read that rule.
mission.objective: Write root-capable.txt with the usernames (one per line, any order, root itself left out) of everyone who can run any command as root on db-01, with or without a password: through their own name, a User_Alias, or membership of a %group in etc/group. Rules limited to certain commands or to another runas user are not full root, and neither are rules for other hosts, commented-out lines or files sudo does not read. Leave the copied files unchanged.

mission.name: Homes Without Owners
mission.description: Before the migration, the files-01 audit needs the home directories to match the account database. `etc/passwd` says where each account's home should be; `home/` is what is on the disk (the sandbox's stand-in for /home).
mission.objective: Write missing.txt with the login names (one per line) of accounts whose home is under /home but whose directory is not in home/, and orphans.txt with the names of the directories in home/ (hidden ones too) that no account has as its home. Then make every existing home directory of an account under /home mode 750, without changing the files inside them. Do not delete anything. Service accounts with homes elsewhere (/var/lib/postgresql, /srv/ftp, ...) are out of scope.

mission.name: Broken Skeleton
mission.description: Every new hire gets a broken shell: their prompt is plain, .profile is missing, and the first thing they find in ~/.ssh is somebody's old key. New accounts start from a copy of /etc/skel. The spec of what a new home must contain is in skel-spec.txt; Dana starts on Monday and alice already has a home from the old skeleton.
mission.objective: Fix etc/skel so it holds exactly the files and modes in skel-spec.txt (take the three dotfile contents from usr/share/base-files/dot.*), then create the account dana with the mock `bin/useradd -m dana` so that home/dana is a copy of the fixed skeleton. Leave alice's existing home as it is. The sandbox's etc/default/useradd already points at etc/skel.
concepts: skeleton is copied at account creation

mission.name: Reports Nobody Can Edit
mission.description: The weekly job publish.sh writes the report into the shared project directory. Teammates in the same group can read the files but not edit them, and they cannot add files to the new folders. Somebody suggested a chmod at the end of the script, but then every new file needs another fix.
mission.objective: Fix publish.sh so that everything it creates (files and directories) can be edited by the group no matter what umask the caller has: new files must come out mode 664 and directories 775 when it runs under umask 077 or 022 alike. Do it with the right umask in the script itself, not with a chmod afterwards, and change nothing else about what it produces.
concepts: umask is per process and inherited

mission.name: Passwords About to Expire
mission.description: Security wants to know which passwords on app-04 expire within 14 days of the ticket date, 2026-11-10, or already have. etc/shadow keeps ageing data as numbers of days since 1970-01-01, and the mock `bin/chage -l USER` prints the same data for one user.
mission.objective: Write expiring.txt with one line `user YYYY-MM-DD` per account whose password expires on or before 2026-11-24, including those already expired, sorted by that date (earliest first). The date is the day the password expires: last change plus maximum age. An account that must change its password at the next login counts as expired now: use the ticket date 2026-11-10 for it. Account expiry dates are not password expiry. Leave etc/shadow unchanged.

mission.name: Who Has No Password?
mission.description: The auditor wants a passwd -S style report for app-04: for every account whether it has a usable password, is locked, or has no password. passwd -S needs root on the live box, so they exported app-04's etc/shadow and etc/passwd into the sandbox. An account with no password is the finding they care about, so they want those listed separately.
mission.objective: Write status.txt with one line per account in etc/shadow, exactly `user P`, `user L` or `user NP` (the codes passwd -S prints: P = usable password, L = locked, NP = no password), and np.txt with the names of the accounts with no password, one per line. Classify each account from the password field of etc/shadow. Leave etc/shadow and etc/passwd unchanged.

mission.name: Shells by Policy
mission.description: The new hardening policy for app-04: service accounts must not have an interactive shell, and nobody may keep a login shell that isn't listed in etc/shells (it breaks chsh, FTP and some PAM checks). Audit etc/passwd and fix it. `bin/usermod -s` is the mock that edits the sandbox's etc/passwd.
mission.objective: Fix the shell field in etc/passwd: every service account (UID 1-999, and nobody) with a login shell gets /usr/sbin/nologin; a person (UID 1000-59999) whose shell is neither listed in etc/shells nor /usr/sbin/nologin nor /bin/false gets /bin/bash. Shells that are already fine stay as they are, including a person who was deliberately disabled with nologin. root and sync (/bin/sync) are exceptions. Every other field and the line order must stay byte-identical, the NIS line included.

mission.name: Environment for Everyone
mission.description: Every login user on app-04 needs the company proxy and JAVA_HOME, including for sftp and scp sessions. The values are in it-notes.txt. On Ubuntu, etc/profile sources the snippets in etc/profile.d/ for every login shell, so that is where a system-wide setting belongs.
mission.objective: Add a snippet to etc/profile.d/ (without editing etc/profile or the existing snippets) so that a clean login shell gets http_proxy, https_proxy and JAVA_HOME exported with the values in it-notes.txt, under both sh (dash) and bash -l. It must print nothing when sourced, and the existing no_proxy setting must stay in effect. The sandbox's etc/profile reads $LM_ETC/profile.d; LM_ETC defaults to $SANDBOX/etc, so `sh -c '. etc/profile; printenv JAVA_HOME'` tests your snippet.

mission.name: scp Breaks on Login
mission.description: Kim on bastion-02 can ssh in fine, but scp and rsync to her account die with "protocol error" or hang. Her ~/.bashrc prints a welcome banner and ends with exec zsh, and every non-interactive ssh command sources it too.
mission.objective: Fix home/kim/.bashrc so that a non-interactive shell prints nothing and carries on: env -i HOME=<her home> bash -c '. ~/.bashrc; echo OK' must print exactly OK. An interactive bash must still print her banner once and define her aliases ll, gs and k, her PATH addition and her EDITOR. Keep every line of her setup; do not delete the banner, the aliases or the exec zsh line.

mission.name: Stale Login Banner
mission.description: Everyone who logs in to bastion-01 is told about a database failover that happened weeks ago, and the banner has no disk-usage line, which the on-call runbook says it must have.
mission.objective: In etc/update-motd.d: keep the stale maintenance script (20-maintenance) in the directory, unchanged, but make it stop running. Add a new script named 50-disk that prints exactly one line, Disk usage (/): NN%, with the percentage that df reports for / (the sandbox's bin/df is the one to ask). Check the result with bin/render-motd: header, system info, disk usage, footer, in that order, nothing else. Leave 00-header, 10-sysinfo and 90-footer alone.

mission.name: Dormant Accounts
mission.description: The quarterly access review wants every dormant account on app-07: people who have not logged in for 90 days or more, or never have. You have the server's passwd and the output of lastlog (lastlog.txt), as of 2026-11-10.
mission.objective: Write dormant.txt with one line per regular account (UID 1000-59999 in etc/passwd) that is dormant, as "<user> <date>" with the last login's date as YYYY-MM-DD in UTC, or "<user> never" if it never logged in. Dormant means the last login, converted to UTC, is on or before 2026-08-12 (90 days before 2026-11-10), or there is no login at all, including accounts that lastlog does not list. System and service accounts are not part of the review. Leave etc/passwd and lastlog.txt unchanged.

mission.name: Offboarding Four Leavers
mission.description: HR sent the leaver list for the end of the month: four people, identified by full name and company email, not by username. Their accounts on app-02 must be locked and expired today, and nothing else may change.
mission.objective: Read TICKET.md and find the four leavers' accounts in etc/passwd (the comment field is the clue). Using the sandbox's usermod, lock each one's password so the original hash stays behind a single ! and set the account expiry to day 1 (shadow field 8). Every other line of etc/shadow, and all of etc/passwd, must stay byte-for-byte as it was. The shared deploy account is on the ticket as 'do not touch'.
concepts: touching only what the ticket names

mission.name: Team Reorg Membership
mission.description: A team reorg moved people between groups on build-05. HR's export is in changes.csv, one add or remove per row, to be applied in order to the server's group databases.
mission.objective: Apply every row of changes.csv, in order, to etc/group and etc/gshadow with the sandbox's gpasswd (add the user to the group, or remove them). The member lists in both files must end up exactly as the rows imply: no stray commas, no duplicates, and no change anywhere else in either file. Rows that ask for something already true (adding a member, removing a non-member) change nothing.
concepts: reading CSV in a shell loop

mission.name: Safe Team Directory
mission.description: The Apollo team has been sharing srv/projects/apollo for a year, and it shows: files in all sorts of modes, some world-writable, some owner-only, nothing inherits the team group. Make it a proper team directory without breaking the tree.
mission.objective: Fix the whole tree under srv/projects/apollo (the directory itself, every subdirectory and every file, hidden ones too). Directories: mode 3770, so new files inherit the group, only the owner can delete other people's files, the team has full access and outsiders none. Regular files: mode 660, except files that currently have any execute bit, which become 770. Symlinks are left alone, and nothing may be deleted, moved or changed outside the tree.

mission.name: Rootless Container IDs
mission.description: Three engineers are getting rootless containers on build-03, which need subordinate UID and GID ranges (etc/subuid and etc/subgid). The files already hold ranges for other people and service accounts, in no particular order.
mission.objective: Give omar, pavel and nina each exactly one range of 65536 IDs in etc/subuid and exactly one in etc/subgid (nina already has one of them: only add what is missing). Every start must be 100000 or higher, and no range may overlap any other range in the same file, existing ones included. Lines that are already in the files stay exactly as they are.

mission.name: Wrong Owners After Restore
mission.description: files/ was restored onto app-09 from the old server's backup with --numeric-owner, so every file carries the old server's UID and GID numbers. The numbers mean different people on app-09. The old server's passwd and group files and a listing of the restored tree (restore-listing.txt) are here.
mission.objective: Write chown-plan.sh in the sandbox: a shell script, run from inside restored/, with one chown line per path that restores the owner BY NAME (user:group, with the names the old server gave those numbers), quoting every path. If only the user or only the group exists on the new server (etc/passwd, etc/group), change just that part (user, or :group); if neither exists, leave the path out. Write unmapped.txt too: one line per owner who appears in the listing but does not exist on the new server, as 'user NAME' or 'group NAME', each once. The sandbox's chown only records what it is asked to do.

mission.name: Who Can Touch What
mission.description: Before granting the audit team access on file-02, the security lead wants to know exactly who can already read and write six files, for five users. The stat output of the six files and of the directories above them was captured in stat.txt, with the server's passwd and group files alongside.
mission.objective: Write matrix.csv with a header line user,path,read,write and one row per user and file (5 users x 6 files = 30 rows), where read and write are yes or no: whether that user can read the file's contents and whether they can modify it, given the owner/group/other rules, group membership including supplementary groups and primary groups, and the directories on the way to the file. The users are kim, tomas, priya, wen and alex; the files are listed in paths.txt. Treat all five as ordinary users (no root, no ACLs).
concepts: directory execute bit and path traversal

mission.name: Onboarding Checklist
mission.description: Three engineers join the platform team on build-07 next week. The onboarding ticket lists everything their accounts need: users, groups, homes, sudo, a forced first password change and container ID ranges. One of them used to work here and still has a locked account.

Nothing else in the account databases may change.

mission.name: Something Is Down
mission.description: The pager fires: "app-02: a service is down". app-02 runs five units of ours: billing-api, order-worker, search-indexer, notify-gateway and the nightly-export job. The on-call runbook says to start with what systemd knows.
mission.objective: Write diagnosis.txt with one line 'UNIT STATUS': the full name of the broken unit (e.g. something.service) and the exit status of its main process, as a number. `systemctl` and `journalctl` are mocks that treat the sandbox as `/`; their output, options and exit codes are the real ones.

mission.name: Back After Reboot
mission.description: During last night's reboot drill on mon-07, every service came back except metrics-agent, and the dashboards have been blank since. The odd part: `systemctl is-enabled metrics-agent` says "enabled".
mission.objective: Make metrics-agent.service start at every boot of this server and get it running now. Don't change the server's default target. `systemctl` and `journalctl` are mocks that treat the sandbox as `/` (/etc/systemd/system is ./etc/systemd/system); they behave like the real tools, including enable's symlinks.

mission.name: Decommission
mission.description: legacy-sync mirrors the file share to the old NAS, and that NAS is being switched off today. The package can't be removed yet (the report team still reads its config), so the change ticket says: legacy-sync must not run now, must not start at boot, and must not be started by anything else.
mission.objective: legacy-sync.service is stopped, not enabled, and masked, so that nothing can start it. Leave the packaged unit file and report.service unchanged, and keep report.service enabled and running. `systemctl` and `journalctl` are mocks that treat the sandbox as `/` (packaged units are in ./usr/lib/systemd/system, local ones in ./etc/systemd/system) and behave like the real tools.

mission.name: Reload, Don't Restart
mission.description: The deploy pipeline just pushed a new etc/api/api.conf (more workers, longer timeout). api.service is in the middle of long export jobs for a customer, and the ticket says: "apply the new config without dropping in-flight jobs".
mission.objective: The running api process (same Main PID as now) must use the new config revision from etc/api/api.conf, and `systemctl reload api` must work for future config changes. `systemctl` and `journalctl` are mocks that treat the sandbox as `/` and run the api as a real background process; the api writes var/log/api/api.log.

mission.name: Since the Window Opened
mission.description: Last night's maintenance on db-04 (kernel update, PostgreSQL restart, reboot) began at 23:40 server time. It is now 03:10 and the change manager wants every serious message logged since then, nothing more, for the post-change review.
mission.objective: Save to errors.txt every journal entry with priority err or more serious (err, crit, alert, emerg) logged since 2026-11-09 23:40 server time, from all units and the kernel, oldest first, in journalctl's short-iso format (one entry per line with ISO date, time and zone). `journalctl` is a mock that reads the journal export in var/log/journal; its clock is frozen at 2026-11-10 03:10 (Europe/Berlin).

mission.name: One Unit, One Window
mission.description: The payment API on pay-01 had an incident last night, and Finance's auditors need its log for exactly the incident window. Ticket: TICKET.txt. pay-01 also runs the EU instance of the same API and a ledger sync job, which log almost the same lines.
mission.objective: Write payment.txt with the message text of every journal entry that belongs to payment.service in the window given in TICKET.txt, oldest first, one per line, without timestamp, host or identifier. That includes everything systemd logged about the unit itself. `journalctl` is a mock that reads the journal export in var/log/journal; its clock is frozen at 2026-11-10 03:10 UTC.

mission.name: Who Crashed Where
mission.description: report-renderer on render-02 keeps dying and getting restarted, and the vendor wants to know exactly when it crashed and in which library. Kernel messages are hidden from normal users there (kernel.dmesg_restrict=1), so a colleague with root captured the ring buffer and /proc/stat into captures/ (see captures/README).
mission.objective: Write crash.txt with one line per segfault recorded in captures/dmesg.txt, oldest first: 'time_utc binary library', for example '2026-11-09T21:14:05Z some-binary libfoo.so.1.2'. time_utc is the wall-clock time of the crash in UTC (ISO 8601 with Z, whole seconds), binary is the crashing program's name, library is the file name the kernel reports the fault in. Don't change the captures.

mission.name: Who Filled the Disk
mission.description: Disk alert on app-02: var/log/syslog grew by gigabytes in the hour from 02:00 to 03:00 and the root filesystem hit 95%. Before anyone turns log levels down, you need to know which programs were that noisy in that hour.
mission.objective: Write top-programs.txt with the three programs that logged the most messages in var/log/syslog between 02:00:00 and 02:59:59 on Nov 10, one per line as 'count program' (e.g. '1234 sshd'), highest count first. A program is the name before [pid] or the colon; count messages, not lines: rsyslog's 'message repeated N times' line stands for N messages. Don't change the log.

mission.name: Did They Get In?
mission.description: Overnight, the monitoring on bastion-1 counted thousands of failed SSH logins. Most brute force fails, but the security team needs to know right now whether any of it worked. Everything is in var/log/auth.log.
mission.objective: Write compromised.txt with one line 'ip user' for every IP address that had at least 5 failed password attempts and, after them, a successful (Accepted) SSH login. user is the account that logged in. Every failed attempt counts, including those rsyslog folded into 'message repeated N times' lines. Any order. Don't change the log.

mission.name: Since the Deploy
mission.description: Since the 14:00 deploy of the shop API, customers have been reporting error pages. Before rolling back, the team lead wants to know which endpoint is hit hardest and how slow its backend got when it failed. The nginx access log is var/log/nginx/access.log; its format is defined in etc/nginx/nginx.conf.
mission.objective: Write worst.txt with one line 'path count max_upstream': among requests logged at 14:00:00 or later, the endpoint path (without the query string) with the most 5xx responses, the number of those 5xx responses, and the highest upstream response time among them in seconds as logged (e.g. '/api/v2/example 12 1.234'). Don't change the log.

mission.name: The File Nobody Writes
mission.description: The disk on app-05 keeps filling up although logrotate runs every night. Since last night's rotation the new var/log/app/app.log has stayed empty while app.log.1 keeps growing, and the old files can't be compressed or removed while the app is still writing to them.
mission.objective: Fix etc/logrotate.d/app so that after every rotation the running app writes its new lines into the new app.log and audit.log and the rotated files stop growing. The app's README forbids copytruncate, and the app should be signalled once per rotation, not once per file. The validator forces a real rotation to check. `systemctl` is a mock that runs the app as a real background process; logrotate is the real one (as non-root, give it a state file with -s).

mission.name: Printed Once
mission.description: The deploy agent prints a one-time admin token into var/log/deploy/deploy.log during each deploy: right after it rotates the log, into the new file, and it scrubs the log again a few seconds later. Last time nobody caught it and the deploy had to be redone. ./trigger-deploy.sh starts a deploy and waits until it has finished.
mission.objective: Run a deploy and save its one-time admin token (adm_ followed by 24 letters and digits) in token.txt. Tip: in the game shell a command ending in & runs in the background (`wait` waits for it, Ctrl-C stops a foreground command).

mission.name: Needle in huge.log
mission.description: orders-api's worker panicked several times today and the developer needs one specific crash (NOTE.txt). huge.log has the whole day: 200,000 lines, far too many to scroll through.
mission.objective: Write to trace.txt the trace id (the 16 hex digits after trace=) from the line that is two lines above the first worker panic (a line containing `panic: `) after the second deploy that really finished (`deploy finished: ...`; dry runs don't count). Don't change huge.log.

mission.name: Wrong Database
mission.description: Config management moved billing to a new database primary (TICKET.txt), but billing.service still connects to the decommissioned pg-legacy-01. The vendor binary takes its settings only from environment variables.
mission.objective: Make billing.service run with the DB_HOST and DB_PORT from TICKET.txt, loaded from etc/billing/env, the file config management owns (keep the values there). Don't modify opt/billing/bin/billing-server. `systemctl` and `journalctl` are mocks that treat the sandbox as /: /etc/billing/env is ./etc/billing/env.

mission.name: Stale Library
mission.description: libssl3 was patched on app-03 an hour ago, but the package never restarts anything. Some of the running services are still using the old, deleted copy of the library from memory (TICKET.md).
mission.objective: Find the services whose process still maps the deleted old libssl and restart exactly those. Write their unit names, one per line (for example api.service), to needs-restart.txt. Restarting services that never used the deleted library is a failure. `systemctl` is a mock (the sandbox is /); the processes are real.
concepts: mapped files vs open file descriptors

mission.name: One Worker per Core
mission.description: render-07 got new hardware this morning, but render-worker still runs with the sizing of the old box. Nobody can log in to look at the CPU right now; the hardware team left a capture of the new box's /proc/cpuinfo in capture/cpuinfo.
mission.objective: Set etc/default/render-worker to the new box: WORKERS = the number of physical CPU cores (hyperthreads don't count), BUILD = avx2 if the CPU supports AVX2, otherwise generic. The file must set only these two (comments are fine). Then make the running render-worker.service use the new values. `systemctl` is a mock that treats the sandbox as /, so /etc/default/... is ./etc/default/...
concepts: physical id / core id / siblings / cpu cores

mission.name: Killed in the Night
mission.description: reports.service died overnight and didn't come back. The on-call note says "OOM?". The runbook (POLICY.md) says how to size the memory limit of a service that the kernel OOM-killed.
mission.objective: Following POLICY.md, set reports.service's MemoryMax to 1.5 × the largest anon-rss of the processes the kernel OOM-killed in reports.service's own cgroup (from the journal), rounded up to the next multiple of 256M, so that `systemctl show -p MemoryMax reports.service` reports it. Then start reports.service again. `systemctl` and `journalctl` are mocks (the journal is in var/log/journal).

mission.name: Restart Storm
mission.description: A 3-second broker blip took queue-consumer down for good: it was restarted so fast that systemd gave up with "Start request repeated too quickly". INC-4471 (TICKET.md) lists what the restart behaviour should be.
mission.objective: Change queue-consumer.service so it follows TICKET.md: restart after failures only (never after a clean exit 0), the RestartSec and start limit (StartLimitBurst / StartLimitIntervalSec) the ticket gives, still enabled. Then get it running again. Don't touch the program. `systemctl` and `journalctl` are mocks (the sandbox is /); the checker replays the broker blip.

mission.name: Which Clock?
mission.description: imgproxy on img-03 was killed by the kernel's OOM killer last night. The alert bot pasted the kernel messages in UTC (kernel-oom.txt), but imgproxy's own log, var/log/imgproxy/app.log, uses the server's local time with no zone. The developer wants the request imgproxy was handling when it died.
mission.objective: Write to match.txt the one line of var/log/imgproxy/app.log that was logged in the same second as the OOM kill (the `Killed process` line in kernel-oom.txt), copied exactly. `timedatectl` is a mock that reports this server's clock and time zone.

mission.name: Hands Off the Vendor Unit
mission.description: The monitoring vendor's agent runs with the vendor's own flags. Change request CHG-2291 (TICKET.md) asks for different flags and one more environment variable, but the unit file belongs to the vendor package and every upgrade overwrites it.
mission.objective: Make vendor-agent run with the flags and the AGENT_CLUSTER variable that TICKET.md asks for, without editing or copying the vendor's unit file in usr/lib/systemd/system, and restart the agent so it runs that way. The vendor's other settings (such as AGENT_LOG=info) must stay. `systemctl` and `journalctl` are mocks (the sandbox is /).
concepts: resetting ExecStart= with an empty assignment

mission.name: From tmux to systemd
mission.description: report-api has been running in a tmux pane that dies every few days. OPS-3318 (TICKET.md) asks for a proper service; notes/tmux-history.txt shows how it is started by hand today.
mission.objective: Write /etc/systemd/system/report-api.service (etc/systemd/system/ here) so that the ticket's requirements hold: it runs report-api on the ticket's port, is enabled for boot, restarts on failure, passes systemd-analyze verify, and is running now under systemd. Don't change /opt/report-api. `systemctl`, `journalctl` and `systemd-analyze` are mocks (the sandbox is /).

mission.name: Start Order
mission.description: After every reboot of web-07, app.service fails because the database proxy is not up yet, and the two should also stop together. OPS-3340 (TICKET.md) lists what the unit files must guarantee.
mission.objective: Fix the unit files in etc/systemd/system so that at boot db-proxy.service starts before app.service, stopping db-proxy.service also stops app.service (but stopping app leaves db-proxy running), and systemd reports no ordering cycle. Keep all three services enabled. `systemctl mock-boot` simulates a boot; `systemctl` and `journalctl` are mocks (the sandbox is /).

mission.name: 502 at 03:10
mission.description: The pager went off at 03:10: the API answers 502. web-02 left you five sources: the live services (mock systemctl), a journal export, the nginx access log, a dmesg capture and a df snapshot (INCIDENT.md). Each keeps time in its own way.
mission.objective: Find what really broke, fix it, and fill in incident.txt (four exact fields: first_error_utc, root_cause_unit, trigger from the listed values, failed_requests) as INCIDENT.md defines them. The unit that caused the incident must run healthy again, and api must be running; don't delete anything that isn't part of the damage. `systemctl` and `journalctl` are mocks (the sandbox is /; journalctl --file reads the export).
concepts: nginx log fields and time zones

mission.name: Four Clocks, One Timeline
mission.description: Postmortem for last night's API outage on web-01. The evidence is in four places that each tell time differently: a journal export (microseconds since the epoch), syslog (local time, no year, no zone), the nginx access log ([10/Nov/2026:03:04:05 +0330]) and the app log (ISO 8601 with offset). rsyslog also copied every journal message into syslog.
mission.objective: Write timeline.txt exactly as TIMELINE-SPEC.txt describes: every event from 03:00:00 to 03:14:59 server local time on Nov 10, one per line as `UTC-TIME SOURCE MESSAGE` (time as 2026-11-09T23:31:05Z, fractions cut off), oldest first; journal entries once (drop their syslog copies), nginx only 5xx, app only WARN/ERROR; events in the same second keep the order journal, syslog, nginx, app and their file order. `timedatectl` and `journalctl` are mocks (journalctl --file reads the export). Don't change the logs.
concepts: syslog has no year or zone

mission.name: What Is On This Disk?
mission.description: A VM lost power during a resize and will not boot. Ops pulled its disk as disk.img and wants an inventory of its partitions before anyone touches it.
mission.objective: Write partitions.txt with one line per data partition on disk.img, in the form: number start_sector size_MiB type_id (for example: 1 2048 100 83). Use the partition numbers the table gives them, the 512-byte start sector, the size in MiB and the hex type id as sfdisk prints it. The extended container is not a data partition and must not be listed. Do not modify disk.img.

mission.name: Plan the Log Volume
mission.description: The app team filed a storage request for a log volume that will hold millions of tiny files. The real disk is not here yet, so you build the volume as an image file to prove the numbers work.
mission.objective: Read REQUEST.txt and build logs.img to match it: the exact size, the file system type, the volume label, the reserved-block percentage and the inode density it asks for. The image must be a clean file system (it passes e2fsck). The shell blocks the mkfs wrapper commands on real devices, but you are working on a plain file: mke2fs does the same job.

mission.name: Fstab After the Disk Swap
mission.description: web-07 has been stuck in emergency mode since a disk swap: etc/fstab still names the old disks. You have a copy of the file and the output of blkid for the new disks.
mission.objective: Edit etc/fstab so that each of its four entries refers to its new disk by UUID= (taken from blkid.txt), the USB backup disk at /mnt/usb-backup no longer blocks boot when it is missing, and the last column is right: pass 1 for the root file system, 0 for swap and 0 or 2 for the others. Keep the comments, the types, the swap mount point and each entry's other options.

mission.name: The Backup That Went Nowhere
mission.description: Backups succeeded all week, yet the USB disk is empty: it was never mounted, and backup.sh wrote into the bare directory on the system disk instead.
mission.objective: Make backup.sh refuse to run (exit non-zero, write nothing) unless its target is a mount point; the check has to call mountpoint through PATH, because the checker substitutes its own. Then move everything that was written into the bare mnt/backup directory, hidden entries included, into stray/, leaving mnt/backup empty. Do not change the files' contents.

mission.name: Same Disk, Two Paths
mission.description: On web-02 the customers' uploads show up under several paths, so the nightly backup of / copies them more than once. You have captures of /proc/mounts and /proc/self/mountinfo.
mission.objective: From mountinfo.txt write binds.txt with one line per bind mount: its mount point and the real source directory it shows, separated by a space, sorted by mount point. Then write backup-excludes.txt for rsync: one anchored directory pattern per line (leading and trailing slash) excluding every bind mount point and none of the originals. Leave the captures unchanged.

mission.name: Put /tmp in RAM
mission.description: CI builds on ci-build-03 are slow because /tmp lives on a disk. The ticket wants a tmpfs there, set up in fstab, plus a figure from the machine you are on.
mission.objective: In etc/fstab replace the disk entry for /tmp by a tmpfs entry with exactly the options TICKET.txt asks for, and leave every other line as it was. Then write shm.txt: the size of this machine's /dev/shm as a plain number of KiB.

mission.name: The 20 GB Backup
mission.description: The weekly backup of two VM images ballooned. One image is a sparse file, the other was written with dd from /dev/zero, and nobody noticed that ls and du disagree about their size.
mission.objective: Following TICKET.txt: write sizes.txt with each original image's apparent size in bytes and allocated size in KiB ("NAME APPARENT_BYTES ALLOCATED_KIB"); create vm2-copy.img, identical to vm/vm2.img but mostly holes; and create vm-backup.tar, a plain tar of vm1.img that stays small and stores the file as a sparse file. The two originals must not be modified.

mission.name: Cut Out Partition 2
mission.description: A vendor wants only the application partition of a disk image. They sent a SHA-256 of exactly what they expect to receive.
mission.objective: Extract partition 2 of disk.img into p2.img so that it is byte-for-byte the partition and matches the checksum in vendor.sha256. Do not modify disk.img.

mission.name: Half-Written Archive
mission.description: A power cut during publish.sh left a truncated latest.tar.gz that the download servers happily served, twice this month.
mission.objective: Rewrite publish.sh so that releases/latest.tar.gz is always either the complete old archive or the complete new one, and the new archive is synced to disk before it gets its public name. The temporary file belongs in the same directory, and the published file must stay mode 644. The checker runs publish.sh with its own tar, sync and mv found through PATH, so call them by plain name. Keep the SRC and DEST variables working.

mission.name: Migrate the Site
mission.description: The site moves to a new server. The copy has to keep permissions, modification times, symlinks and hard links, and the team wants proof that nothing is left to sync.
mission.objective: Copy www/ to new-server/www/ so that it is an exact copy: file types, permissions (including setuid and sticky bits), modification times, symlinks as links and hard links between files. Then run the same copy again as a listing only (itemized, changing nothing) and save its output in second-run.txt, which must be empty. Do not create a nested www/www.
concepts: hard links and symlinks in copies

mission.name: Mirror Without Mercy
mission.description: The public mirror still serves releases that were pulled at the source. It must become an exact copy of releases/, but the mirror admin keeps private notes inside it.
mission.objective: Make mirror/ an exact copy of releases/ (removing everything that no longer exists there, updating changed files and links) while mirror/.local-notes/ stays untouched. Before changing anything, save a dry run in plan.txt containing exactly the "*deleting" lines that the real run carries out, and nothing else.
concepts: protecting paths with --exclude or filter rules

mission.name: Deleted but Still There
mission.description: A 2 GB dump was deleted to free space, but df did not change: the data has other names scattered around the tree.
mission.objective: Remove every extra name (hard link) of the data in data/big.dat so that it is the file's only name and its link count is 1. Keep the data itself. Separate copies that merely have identical content, a different file with the same name, and links between unrelated files must stay exactly as they are.

mission.name: Links that Can Move
mission.description: A shop's app/ tree was restored to a new path from the dead host, and its symbolic links still point at absolute paths of the old machine.
mission.objective: Make every symlink in app/ that points inside the old tree a relative link that reaches the same file or directory, so the tree still works when copied anywhere. Links that point at other places on the system must stay exactly as they are, and no files or extra links may be added.

mission.name: No Space, Plenty of Space
mission.description: Logins on web-01 fail with "No space left on device" although df shows the disk less than half full.
mission.objective: Write the path of the directory that holds the most files, relative to the level folder, into hog.txt. Then delete the expired PHP session files in it (sess_* files not modified for more than 24 hours). Fresh sessions and everything else in the tree must stay untouched.

mission.name: Reading the Quota Report
mission.description: The NAS is running out of room for the team. The repquota capture says who is in trouble, and a change ticket asks for two users' limits to be raised.
mission.objective: From the NAS report, write into over.txt the users over a soft limit whose grace period is still running (and not at a hard limit), and into hard.txt the users who cannot write any more (at a hard limit, or grace expired). Then apply the two limit changes from TICKET.txt with setquota (a stand-in for the real tool is provided in bin/), leaving everything else as it is. One name per line.

mission.name: Names That Stay Put
mission.description: After a reboot /dev/sdb1 and /dev/sdc1 traded places and the backup job wrote onto the live data disk. The file systems need names that survive a reshuffle.
mission.objective: Find out which of data.img and backup.img really holds the shop's live data and which the nightly backups (do not trust file names or current labels). Label the first DATA and the second BACKUP without reformatting, then change etc/fstab so /srv/data is mounted by LABEL=DATA and /srv/backup by LABEL=BACKUP, keeping all other fields and lines unchanged.

mission.name: What Is in the Box?
mission.description: Finance dropped a box of unlabeled disk images on the team: some ext file systems, a swap area, a partitioned disk and one that looks empty.
mission.objective: Write inventory.csv (first line file,TYPE,UUID,LABEL) with one row per image in images/, as blkid sees the contents, not the names. An image with a partition table gets one row per partition named FILE@p1, FILE@p2, and none for the whole disk; an image with nothing recognisable gets a row with empty TYPE, UUID and LABEL. Fields an image does not have stay empty.

mission.name: Ship It with a Manifest
mission.description: The release set in backup/ goes to the restore team, who will verify it file by file against a manifest you have to produce.
mission.objective: Write MANIFEST.tsv next to backup/ (not inside it): tab-separated, no header, one row per regular file (path, size in bytes, octal mode, sha256) and one row per symlink (path, the word symlink, its target), paths as find prints them inside backup/ (starting with ./), hidden files included, all rows in LC_ALL=C byte order. Do not change the tree.

mission.name: Trust, but Verify
mission.description: The shop was restored onto the new box, and last night's manifest is the only proof of what should be there.
mission.objective: Compare restored/ against MANIFEST.tsv (path, size, mode, sha256) and write verify-report.txt with three sections in this order, each header alone on a line followed by one ./-style path per line in byte order: == MISSING == (in the manifest, not on disk), == EXTRA == (regular files on disk the manifest does not list), == CORRUPTED == (present but with different content). Files that only changed mode or timestamp are not corrupted. Do not modify restored/.

mission.name: Restore Without Overwriting
mission.description: An accidental rm on Tuesday removed several files and a directory from projects/, and the team has been editing other files since Monday's backup.
mission.objective: Restore from backups/projects-mon.tar.gz only what was deleted from projects/, with the content, permissions and modification times it had in the backup. Files that still exist (edited or not) and files created since Monday must stay exactly as they are, and nothing outside the backup's contents may appear.

mission.name: Snapshots that Share
mission.description: The nightly full copy of site/ is filling the backup disk, although most files never change from one day to the next.
mission.objective: Take snapshots/day1 of site/, run ./change-day.sh once, then take snapshots/day2. Both must look like complete copies (same contents, modes and modification times); files identical in the two days must be stored once (same inode), changed files separately, deleted files absent from day2, and no snapshot may share files with the live site/.

mission.name: Grandfather, Father, Son
mission.description: Nobody ever pruned the database dumps: backups/ holds over a year of db-YYYY-MM-DD.tar.zst files, with gaps, odd files and a db-latest symlink among them.
mission.objective: Write prune.sh to apply the retention policy in POLICY.txt (7 daily, 4 weekly, 12 monthly, TODAY taken from the environment). Without arguments it is a dry run that prints would delete NAME for each file and removes nothing; with --apply it deletes them; any other argument prints usage and exits 2. Files that are not valid backup names, including the db-latest.tar.zst symlink, are never touched. The checker runs your script on several fixtures with different TODAY values.

mission.name: Retention with a Paper Trail
mission.description: Compliance has issued a data retention policy for the shared data/ directory: logs, PII exports and invoices each have their own clock, and legal holds override them.
mission.objective: Write retention.sh that applies POLICY.txt to the data/ directory next to it (compress logs older than 7 days keeping their modification time, delete logs older than 90 days, delete PII exports older than 30 days unless the file name is on the legal hold list, delete invoices after 7 years, touch nothing else) and appends one COMPRESS/DELETE line per action to retention.log. Run it here. A second run must change nothing, and the checker also runs your script on a fresh copy of the data.

mission.name: The 3 a.m. Bundle
mission.description: On-call needs a self-contained disaster-recovery bundle for shop-01 that can be shipped through a transfer tool with a 20 MB part limit and verified on arrival.
mission.objective: Build out/dr-bundle.tgz.part-aa, -ab, ... (parts of at most 20,000,000 bytes) of a gzip tar holding the directory dr-bundle with files/ (every path of bundle.list from box/, links replaced by their target's content), fstab, disk.sfdisk (the dump of disk.img) and MANIFEST.sha256 (relative paths, verifiable after extraction), plus out/SHA256SUMS for the parts. out/ holds only those. TICKET.txt has the exact layout; the checker joins, extracts, verifies and replays the partition table.

mission.name: Five Schedules
mission.description: The ops lead wants five monitoring checks for the new status page and wrote the schedules in plain English in ticket.txt. Before anything gets the real scripts, the schedules have to be right.
mission.objective: Write schedule.cron with one crontab line per schedule in ticket.txt, in the ticket's order, each running the command true. Each line must fire at exactly the times its schedule describes, no more and no fewer. cron-expand (a LinuxMissions helper, not a standard tool) lists when crontab lines would fire.

mission.name: One More Job
mission.description: You are logged in as deploy. The product team wants the page cache warmed every night before the European morning, and deploy's crontab already holds six jobs that other people depend on.
mission.objective: Add a job to deploy's installed crontab that runs /opt/app/bin/warm-cache --all every day at 04:10. The six jobs already in the table, and every other line in it, must stay exactly as they are. In this sandbox crontab is a mock (bin/crontab, first on your PATH) that keeps tables in var/spool/cron/crontabs/ instead of the system's.

mission.name: The Backup That Never Ran
mission.description: Last month someone dropped db-backup.sh into etc/cron.daily so the database would be dumped every morning. var/backups/ is still empty, and the cron log shows cron.daily running every day.
mission.objective: Make run-parts pick up the database backup in etc/cron.daily, so the daily cron run (06:25, `run-parts --report etc/cron.daily`) really runs it and it writes var/backups/db-<date>.sql.gz. Keep the script's code and its #!/bin/sh line working, keep exactly one copy of it, and leave the other cron.daily scripts as they are.

mission.name: The Percent Sign
mission.description: Yesterday someone changed the hourly report job in deploy's crontab.txt so every report gets its own dated file name. Since then no report has been written, and every hour cron mails deploy an error (var/mail/deploy).
mission.objective: Fix the hourly report line in crontab.txt so that every run, at minute 0 of each hour, writes the output of app/report.sh to reports/report-YYYY-MM-DD-HH.txt (the date and hour of that run). Leave the other lines of crontab.txt and app/report.sh unchanged. cron-run is a LinuxMissions mock that runs a crontab on a simulated clock with cron's real rules, for example: cron-run --crontab crontab.txt --from "2025-06-10 09:00" --to "2025-06-10 11:00" --summary

mission.name: Wrong Hour in the Queue
mission.description: Before going on leave, a colleague queued three one-shot jobs on the shared dbadmin account for the database maintenance (change-ticket.txt). One of them restarts the main database at 15:00 today, in the middle of business hours, instead of 03:00 tomorrow.
mission.objective: Fix dbadmin's at queue: the main database restart must no longer run at 15:00 today and must be queued exactly once for 03:00 tomorrow (Thu 2025-09-18), with the same command. The other two jobs must keep their job numbers and times. at, atq and atrm are mocks here (in bin/, first on your PATH): they keep the spool in var/spool/cron/atjobs, their clock is frozen at Wed 2025-09-17 11:20, and jobs never really run.

mission.name: When the Box Is Idle
mission.description: Rebuilding the search index with app/reindex.sh pins the CPU for an hour, so RUNBOOK.txt says it must never be started by hand: it goes through batch, which starts it once the load is low. The last person who tried got a job that died at 2 a.m.
mission.objective: Queue exactly one batch job (queue b) that runs app/reindex.sh in such a way that, when atd starts it later, reindex.sh runs with app/ as its working directory and DATA_DIR set to the sandbox's data directory (the full path), and completes. batch, at, atq and atrm are mocks here (in bin/, first on your PATH); they keep jobs in var/spool/cron/atjobs exactly like atd and never run them on their own.
concepts: working directory of an at job

mission.name: From Cron to Timer
mission.description: The team is moving the app server's jobs from cron to systemd timers. Next on the list is the purge job in crontab.txt: `30 2 * * 1-5 /opt/app/purge.sh`. Unlike cron, the timer should also catch up on a run that was missed while the server was down.
mission.objective: Write etc/systemd/system/purge.service and etc/systemd/system/purge.timer. The service runs /opt/app/purge.sh. The timer starts purge.service at exactly the times the cron line did (02:30, Monday to Friday), runs a missed start after downtime, and is enabled through timers.target. bin/systemd-analyze is a mock that supports only the calendar verb.

mission.name: Survive the Hangup
mission.description: migrate.sh copies the orders table to the new database cluster, batch by batch, for about four hours. Your VPN drops every evening, and when the terminal goes away, so does everything started from it.
mission.objective: Start one copy of migrate.sh so that it keeps running when the terminal hangs up (it must ignore SIGHUP) and its output (stdout and stderr) goes to logs/migrate.log, not to the terminal and not to nohup.out. The check sends the running migration a real SIGHUP. Linux only (it reads /proc): on macOS play with --docker.

mission.name: Pause, Snapshot, Resume
mission.description: export.sh streams the orders archive to the backup disk for about a minute. The DBA needs a consistent snapshot of that disk right now, and snapshot.sh refuses to run while anything is writing to it. Nobody wants to restart the export from the beginning.
mission.objective: Start export.sh as a background job, pause it, run snapshot.sh while it is paused, then let the same export continue in the background until it writes DONE to export.log. The check reads export.log and snapshot.log: one export run must contain a pause, the whole snapshot must fall inside that pause, and the export's heartbeat counter must continue where it stopped. Linux only: on macOS play with --docker.

mission.name: Three Shards, Three Answers
mission.description: The nightly customer import is split into three shards (eu, us, apac). They have to run at the same time to fit the window, and the change ticket asks for each shard's exit status, because 3 and 4 mean very different things for the morning team (see README.txt).
mission.objective: Run ./import.sh eu, ./import.sh us and ./import.sh apac at the same time, as background jobs of your shell, wait for them, and write each shard's exit status to statuses.txt as three lines shard=status (for example eu=0). The check reads the shards' own logs: the three runs must overlap in time, and statuses.txt must hold the codes they really returned.

mission.name: Cut the Cord
mission.description: The order-queue consumer keeps dying: last week a Ctrl-C meant for another command took it down, and before that a closed SSH session did. It has to run completely apart from any terminal.
mission.objective: Start exactly one consumer.sh that is fully detached: it leads its own session (its session id equals its PID), has no controlling terminal (TTY ?), reads stdin from /dev/null, and appends its stdout and stderr to logs/consumer.log. It must keep processing messages: the check drops one into queue/ and expects it in done/ within a few seconds. Linux only (it reads /proc): on macOS play with --docker.

mission.name: Wait for Ready
mission.description: The deploy hook runs the smoke tests right after starting the app, and half the time the app is not listening yet, so the deploy fails for nothing. ./probe tells whether the app is ready (exit 0) or not yet (exit 1).
mission.objective: Write an executable wait_ready.sh that runs ./probe every 2 seconds until it succeeds, then exits 0. It gives up after a timeout in seconds, taken from its first argument (default 30), and then exits 1. It must react within 2 seconds of the app becoming ready, and must not call ./probe more often than every 2 seconds. The check runs your script against an app that becomes ready after a few seconds and against one that never does (with a short timeout), so it takes about 10 seconds after each change to the script.

mission.name: Drain Then Switch
mission.description: Upload traffic moves from eu-west-1 to eu-west-2 tonight (CHANGE.txt). The uploader is paused with a full queue in spool/, and the load balancer gives you a 5-second window once the queue is empty.
mission.objective: Resume the uploader with ./resume-uploads.sh; it empties spool/ in the background within about a minute. Run ./switch-traffic.sh once spool/ has no entries left at all (files still being uploaded count): not before, and no more than 5 seconds after. If you miss the window, type reset to refill the queue.

mission.name: Hanging Healthchecks
mission.description: The nightly fleet report never finishes: ./healthcheck.sh HOST hangs forever for some hosts, and the loop over hosts.txt waits on it (NOTE.txt).
mission.objective: Write report.txt with one line per host, in the order of hosts.txt: the host name, a space, and OK (the check passed), FAIL (it returned an error) or TIMEOUT (no answer within 3 seconds). Every host must be checked with ./healthcheck.sh, each check may run at most 3 seconds, and no healthcheck.sh process may be left running.

mission.name: One At A Time
mission.description: Cron starts sync.sh every minute, but since the supplier feed grew a sync takes about 90 seconds. Two imports now write into catalog.db at the same time and corrupt it (INCIDENT.txt, crontab.txt).
mission.objective: Change sync.sh so a copy that finds another sync still running exits with a non-zero status at once, with a message on its output, without touching catalog.db. The exclusion must survive a run killed with kill -9, and its lock file must live in this directory. Keep the SYNC_SECONDS line; the checker uses it to shorten the sync.

mission.name: The Log That Won't Let Go
