mission.description: app.log is huge and still growing, and the application that writes it cannot be restarted: it opened the file once and keeps it open (TICKET.txt). A scaled-down copy of the problem is in this directory.
mission.objective: Write logrotate.conf for $SANDBOX/app.log: keep 5 old logs, the newest app.log.1 uncompressed and the older ones gzipped. Then rotate right now with the state file logrotate.state in this directory. The running writer must not be stopped, and afterwards its new lines must appear in app.log, not in app.log.1.

mission.name: Sunday Freeze
mission.description: Storage maintenance owns Sunday from 01:00 to 04:00 and nothing else may run then. The team's crontab.txt (storage-ops on stor-02) has twenty lines, and the schedules are not all as simple as they look.
mission.objective: In crontab.txt, put the prefix `#FREEZE ` (with the space) in front of every job line that can fire on any Sunday of the next 12 months at a minute from 01:00 to 03:59, using cron's real rules. Do not change, add or remove anything else: every other line must stay byte-identical.

mission.name: The Backup Calendar
mission.description: The file server's one-line backup crontab runs incrementals every day, Sundays and month starts included, on top of the other backups. The new calendar is in BACKUP-PLAN.txt and has to be written as cron lines for review.
mission.objective: Write backup.cron with the jobs from BACKUP-PLAN.txt, each calling this directory's backup.sh with its mode (incremental, full, archive). Incremental: 01:30 Monday to Saturday, but not on the 1st. Full: 01:30 every Sunday. Archive: 03:00 on the 1st. A simulated cron run of about two months must produce exactly these runs. Do not install the file.

mission.name: The Cleanup That Ate The Server
mission.description: A nightly cleanup job wiped web-03's uploads when its CACHE_DIR variable went missing from the crontab (POSTMORTEM.txt). The job is one `find` line with no safety net.
mission.objective: Rewrite cleanup.sh. With CACHE_DIR set to a directory it deletes only regular files below it whose last change is more than 7 days ago; it keeps every .keep file, every directory and every symlink, and never touches what a symlink points to. With CACHE_DIR unset, empty or not a directory it prints a reason on stderr, exits non-zero and deletes nothing. File names may contain spaces, leading dashes and newlines. It must stay executable.

mission.name: Reports Nobody Reads
mission.description: The daily sales report job runs under cron, but its output never arrives anywhere, its warnings vanish, and a missing feed went unnoticed (TICKET.txt). The job line is in crontab.txt.
mission.objective: Fix crontab.txt (do not install it, and don't edit report.sh or salesagg): one job at 06:30 every day, with MAILTO=ops@example.com set before it. A good run keeps all of its output, report and warnings, in $SANDBOX/logs/report-YYYY-MM-DD.log and sends no mail; when report.sh fails, cron mails ops. It must work under cron's PATH of /usr/bin:/bin. bin/cron-run is a mock cron for testing.

mission.name: Four Silent Timers
mission.description: After the web server was rebuilt, the night housekeeping stopped: four of the eleven systemd timers copied into etc/systemd/system never fire (MIGRATION.txt). Nobody knows which ones or why.
mission.objective: Find the four broken timers, list them in broken.txt (one name per line, like cert-renew.timer), and fix each with the smallest change: every timer ends up with a valid OnCalendar (or another trigger), an existing service to start, and a [Install] section with WantedBy=timers.target. The seven working timers must stay byte-identical. bin/systemd-analyze is a mock that supports only the calendar verb.

mission.name: The Box That Sleeps At Night
mission.description: The build box bb-02 is switched off every night from 22:00 to 07:00, so its 02:00 nightly build in crontab.txt silently skips. boot-history.txt is the box's `last -x` output (TICKET.txt has the details, including a crash).
mission.objective: Write missed.txt: the dates, as YYYY-MM-DD one per line, among the last 14 nightly runs (2026-10-28 to 2026-11-10) on which the box was down at 02:00. Then move the nightly job to anacrontab as exactly one new line that runs it every day, 5 to 15 minutes after anacron starts, with a unique job identifier and the full original command, and remove it from crontab.txt. Leave the other lines of both files alone.

mission.name: Night Shift Handover
mission.description: The night team wants one list of everything that will run by itself on app-07: crontabs of several kinds, systemd timers and queued at jobs live in five different places (HANDOVER.txt).
mission.objective: Write inventory.tsv with one tab-separated row per really scheduled item and the columns source, user, schedule, command (the exact definitions are in HANDOVER.txt), no header, any order. Leave out comments, blank lines, VAR=value lines, disabled timers and files cron ignores. bin/atq and bin/at (for at -c) are mocks of the real tools.

mission.name: Monday's Batch Window
mission.description: Monday's batch window (00:00 to 06:00) keeps colliding: the DB backup runs while the reindex holds its locks, and the sales report starts before the order export has finished (PLAN.txt). The real runtimes are in durations.log.
mission.objective: Reschedule the heavy jobs in crontab.txt (heavy = p95 runtime of 30 minutes or more, measured from durations.log, definition in PLAN.txt) so that on Monday every heavy line fires once in the window, each heavy run finishes by 06:00, no two heavy runs overlap, and report-sales starts only after export-orders has finished. Only the minute and hour fields of heavy lines may change; every other line stays exactly as it is. bin/cron-expand lists fire times.

mission.name: Unprotected Private Key
mission.description: A teammate copied the deploy user's home folder from a USB stick and now `ssh -i home/.ssh/id_ed25519 ...` refuses to work with "UNPROTECTED PRIVATE KEY FILE". The permissions did not survive the trip.
mission.objective: Lock down home/.ssh the way OpenSSH demands: the folder itself private to its owner, every private key readable and writable by the owner only, public keys world-readable, and authorized_keys and config private to the owner. Do not change file contents and do not touch anything else under home/.

mission.name: Never Loosen
mission.description: The security policy in policy.txt caps the permissions of everything in app/. The files were copied around by several people and many are too open, but a few secrets were already locked down harder than the policy requires.
mission.objective: Bring every file under app/ in line with policy.txt without ever making a file more permissive than it is now: a file must end up with exactly the permissions it has now minus whatever the policy does not allow. Leave file contents and folder modes alone.

mission.name: Capital X
mission.description: The release tarball for the app's config tree, etc-app/, was extracted from a build box with a sloppy umask: group and others can write almost everything. Services still need to read it and enter its folders, and the helper scripts must still run.
mission.objective: Fix etc-app/ recursively: nobody but the owner may write anywhere, everybody may read every file and enter every folder, and the scripts keep their execute permission for everyone. Plain data files must not become executable, and file contents stay as they are.

mission.name: Files That Vanish
mission.description: Users of the shared upload areas under srv/ complain that their files keep disappearing: somebody else deleted them. A shared folder that everyone can write to lets everyone delete anything in it unless the sticky bit is set.
mission.objective: Set the sticky bit on every world-writable directory under srv/ that does not have it yet, and change nothing else: directories that already have it, directories that are not world-writable and all files keep their modes. Write the paths of the directories you fixed, one per line, to fixed.txt.

mission.name: Wrong Group
mission.description: Files created in the team's projects/ tree get the creator's personal group, so colleagues in the team group cannot edit them. The directories should hand their group down to everything created inside them.
mission.objective: Make every directory under projects/ (including projects/ itself, hidden directories and directories with spaces in their names) pass its group on to new files and subdirectories. Do not put that special bit on regular files, and keep every other permission bit exactly as it is.

mission.name: Who Gave That Root?
mission.description: A hardened image was delivered with a baseline of the setuid and setgid programs the vendor expects. Someone suspects that other programs on the image can run with elevated rights. The image's file system is unpacked under rootfs/.
mission.objective: Find every file under rootfs/ that has the setuid or setgid bit and is not listed in suid-baseline.txt (the baseline paths are written as seen from inside the image, starting with /). Write those paths in the same style, one per line, to unexpected.txt, and remove both special bits from exactly those files without changing their other permissions. Files in the baseline must keep their bits.

mission.name: The Race Before chmod
mission.description: issue-cert.sh creates a private key file and then runs chmod 600 on it. Between the two commands the key exists with whatever mode the caller's umask allows, so on a busy host another user can read it in that gap.
mission.objective: Change issue-cert.sh so the private key (and the directories it creates) are never accessible to other users, even for a moment, whatever umask the caller has. The script must keep printing exactly the same output and still produce the key, the request and the certificate.

mission.name: First Match Wins
mission.description: The pentest report says this server still accepts root logins and password logins and allows ten authentication attempts per connection. Yet etc/ssh/sshd_config already says PermitRootLogin no. sshd's own view of the configuration is what counts, and you have a stand-in for it: `sshd -T -f etc/ssh/sshd_config` prints the effective settings (add `-C user=NAME,host=HOST,addr=IP` to see them for one connection).
mission.objective: Change the configuration under etc/ssh/ so that the effective settings are PermitRootLogin no, PasswordAuthentication no and MaxAuthTries 3, for every user including deploy and from every address. Everything else that is configured today (including the special rules for the backup user and for the internal network) must stay effective exactly as it is, and `sshd -t -f etc/ssh/sshd_config` must still pass.

mission.name: Host Key Changed
mission.description: git.internal was rebuilt overnight and ssh now shouts "REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED" (see ssh-error.txt). The team's known_hosts file hashes its host names, so grep cannot tell you which lines belong to the server. The new host keys were collected on the trusted console with ssh-keyscan and saved in keyscan.txt.
mission.objective: In known_hosts, remove the old keys of git.internal, including the ones stored under its alternate address [10.4.0.7]:2222, and make the new keys from keyscan.txt the trusted keys for git.internal. Every entry for other hosts must stay in the file byte for byte.

mission.name: Offboarding Day
mission.description: Three people left the company on Friday; offboard.txt lists their key fingerprints. The deploy account's authorized_keys still contains their keys, and the CI system's key can do far more than it should: it is a bare key with no restrictions at all.
mission.objective: Edit authorized_keys: remove exactly the keys whose fingerprints are in offboard.txt, leave every other key line unchanged, and restrict the CI key (comment ci-deploy@runner) so that it can only run /usr/local/bin/deploy-only, only from the 10.0.0.0/8 network, with port forwarding and a terminal disallowed. The file must still be accepted by `ssh-keygen -lf authorized_keys`.

mission.name: Which Mirror Can You Trust
mission.description: agent-2.3.1.tar.gz was downloaded from four mirrors, each with a detached .sig file. The vendor's release key is in vendor.gpg. Mirrors are run by third parties, so only a verified copy may be installed.
mission.objective: Check every copy against vendor.gpg without a full GnuPG setup. Move the one copy with a valid signature from the vendor's release key into verified/ (the folder is empty now) and delete the other three tarballs. Write report.txt with one line per mirror, `<mirror-name> good` or `<mirror-name> bad`.

mission.name: Checksums That Won't Check
mission.description: You pulled part of a release from a mirror into release/, together with the vendor's SHA256SUMS. That list covers many more files than you downloaded and its lines are not all in the same shape, so a plain check does not cover every file. One of the files you downloaded is corrupted.
mission.objective: Verify every downloaded file that SHA256SUMS covers. Save sha256sum's own per-file OK/FAILED lines in verify.log (in the sandbox folder, not in release/), and move the corrupted file into quarantine/. Do not touch the files that verified correctly.

mission.name: Before the Contractor Logs In
mission.description: A contractor gets a shell on this box on Monday. Before that, someone has to check home/ for anything that would let another local user read the owner's secrets or take over the account.
mission.objective: Audit home/ (every file and directory below it, hidden ones included). Fix each path that other users could read but should not (credential files, the .ssh folder and its private key) so that only the owner has access, and each path that group or others can write but should not (startup files, scripts and folders that run as the owner), so that they lose that write access. List every path you fixed, one per line as home/..., in findings.txt. Do not change anything else: files meant to be public must keep their modes.

mission.name: Before the Repo Goes Public
mission.description: A snapshot of the billing-sync repository in repo/ will be published tomorrow. Over the years people committed AWS keys, a private key, passwords and tokens, some of them in hidden folders and old compressed logs.
mission.objective: Find every real credential under repo/ (hidden folders and .gz files included) and write one `file:line` per leak to leaks.txt, for example `repo/config/x.ini:7` (for a .gz file the line number is the line in the decompressed text; for a private key, the BEGIN line). Real credentials are: AWS access key ids (AKIA followed by 16 capitals or digits), private key blocks, `password` settings (any case, with or without spaces around `=`) that have a real value, and GitHub tokens that start with `ghp_`. Documented placeholders, empty values, `<...>` and `${...}` values and settings that merely contain the word password are not leaks. Do not edit anything in repo/ yet: the line numbers must stay valid.

mission.name: The Password Everyone Can See
mission.description: Two worker processes run on this shared box, started by app/start-worker.sh and by a second script. Any local user can run ps. One of the workers exposes its database password that way.
mission.objective: Find out which worker leaks the database password and write its original PID to leak.txt. Then change app/start-worker.sh so the password is no longer in the script or on the command line: it must be read from secrets/db.pass (mode 600; the worker accepts a PASSWORD_FILE environment variable naming a file). Stop the leaking worker and start it again with the fixed script until logs/NAME.log shows it connected. The worker that was not leaking must keep running untouched, and no running process may show the password anywhere on its command line.

mission.name: Typed It in Plain Text
mission.description: Somebody typed a database password and an API token straight into the shell, and bash dutifully saved every command in home/.bash_history. That file gets backed up and shared with the support team.
mission.objective: Remove from home/.bash_history every line that exposes a secret: database commands with the password typed on the line (after -p, with or without a space before it, or as --password=) and exports of API_TOKEN or of a *_PASSWORD variable. Keep every other line, in the original order (commands that only mention the word password, or that make mysql ask for the password, are harmless), and keep the file's mode. Then configure home/.bashrc so that an interactive shell never saves a command whose first character is a space.

mission.name: The Predictable Temp File
mission.description: nightly-report.sh builds its report in $TMPDIR/report.tmp, a name every user can guess, and removes it on its last line. On a shared server another user can plant a symlink there and make the job overwrite any file the job's owner can write.
mission.objective: Fix nightly-report.sh (usage: ./nightly-report.sh data/sales.csv out.txt). Its work file must be created safely, must not be readable by other users while it exists, and must be removed when the script ends, whether it succeeds or stops with an error half way. The report itself must stay exactly the same and the script must still fail on malformed data.

mission.name: Six Teams, Six Doors to Root
mission.description: Six teams have rules in etc/sudoers.d/. The security review found that some of them look narrow but let the user become root anyway: shell escapes, wildcards that accept extra arguments, scripts the user can edit. ownership.txt is the output of stat for the scripts the rules mention.
mission.objective: Find the rules in etc/sudoers.d/ that give a user a way to become root (only files sudo actually reads count, and etc/sudoers is out of scope). Write each one as `etc/sudoers.d/FILE:LINE` (its line number before you change anything) to escalations.txt, one per line. Then rewrite those rules into safe forms that still let the team do its task: reading logs, editing a config file, restarting its service, running the backup, deploying. The platform team provides root-owned wrappers /usr/local/sbin/backup-home and /usr/local/sbin/deploy-release. No rule may grant a shell, editor, pager, find, tar, a wildcard argument or an unprotected script; every file must still pass `visudo -cf`, and the rules that were already safe must remain.

mission.name: Whose tar Is It?
mission.description: The root cron job srv/rotate-keys.sh archives the service keys every night. It calls tar and gzip by plain name, and the cron file etc/cron.d/rotate-keys hands it a PATH that starts with a directory every user can write to.
mission.objective: Find the directory in the job's PATH that any local user can write to and write its path to hijack.txt. Then fix srv/rotate-keys.sh so that nobody can substitute their own tar or gzip, whatever directory the job is started from and whatever PATH it inherits. The script must keep printing the same two lines and keep producing the same archive. Do not rely on changing the cron file.

mission.name: Who Still Needs the Patch
mission.description: The security team published a notice with the fixed versions of bash, openssl, sudo and libc6 (advisory.txt). Eight hosts reported their packages with `dpkg-query -W`, one file per host in fleet/.
mission.objective: Write vulnerable.tsv: one line for every host that has bash, openssl, sudo or libc6 installed at a version older than the fixed one, with four tab-separated fields: host (the file name without .txt), package (as named in the advisory, without any :arch suffix), installed version, fixed version. Hosts that do not have the package are not vulnerable, and neither are look-alike packages such as bash-completion or sudo-ldap. Versions must be compared the way Debian does it (epochs and ~ included).

mission.name: A Service That Cannot Rewrite Itself
mission.description: The report generator reportd runs as the login user jalil, with a bash shell, and its own code under opt/reportd is writable by that user (and partly by everybody). If the service is ever exploited, the attacker can change its code and log in as a real person. The sandbox is a small fake root: etc/passwd and etc/group are its account files, and etc/systemd/system/reportd.service is the unit.
mission.objective: Harden reportd. (1) Create a dedicated system account reportd (its own group, a system UID below 1000, shell /usr/sbin/nologin, home /var/lib/reportd, not under /home) with the useradd stand-in in bin/. (2) Make the unit run as it and sandbox it: no way to gain new privileges, the whole file system read-only except its state directory /var/lib/reportd (and only that), a private /tmp and no access to home directories. (3) Nothing under opt/reportd may be writable by the service user, while it must still be able to read its config and run its script; /var/lib/reportd must be writable by it and not by everybody. Ownership cannot really change in a sandbox: the chown in bin/ records it (`chown --list` shows the records; unlisted files belong to jalil). `bin/reportd-check` is a dry run of the service under the unit's settings and `bin/systemd-analyze verify` checks the unit file.

mission.name: Quarterly Audit, Read Only
mission.description: It is quarter end, and the security officer wants one list of everything wrong on the mock server in host/ before any fixing starts. policy.txt defines each category of finding and categories.txt holds the names to use. The sshd stand-in in bin/ answers `sshd -T -f host/etc/ssh/sshd_config` like the real one.
mission.objective: Write audit.tsv with one line per finding and three tab-separated fields: category, path (relative, like host/etc/...), detail, exactly as policy.txt describes each category. Cover world-writable files, unexpected SUID/SGID files, private keys with a weak mode, effective sshd settings that break the policy and plaintext secrets. This is an audit: do not change anything under host/ (a hash of the tree is checked).

mission.name: What Did They Leave Behind
mission.description: The account deploy was compromised last night. You have its home (home/deploy), the SSH log var/log/auth.log and the shell history. The attacker did not just look around: they planted ways to come back. The crontab of deploy is kept in a mock spool: use `bin/crontab -l` to read it and `bin/crontab -` or `bin/crontab FILE` to replace it.
mission.objective: Find every persistence mechanism the attacker left behind and remove it: a key in authorized_keys, a scheduled job in deploy's crontab, a change to the shell startup file home/deploy/.bashrc and a copy of a shell with the setuid bit under home/. Leave every legitimate key, cron job, alias and setuid program in place (usr/bin/passwd is legitimate), and keep the log and history as evidence. Then write the attacker's IP address and the fingerprint (SHA256:...) of the key they added, one per line, to iocs.txt, without any IP address or fingerprint that belongs to a legitimate user, to the scanner that only failed to log in, or to a legitimate key.

mission.name: Twelve Points Before Go-Live
mission.description: The new bastion image in image/ must pass the 12-point checklist in CHECKLIST.md before it goes live. Some points are already fine, most are not, and the auditor will check all twelve every time. The sshd stand-in in bin/ reports the effective configuration (`sshd -T -f image/etc/ssh/sshd_config`, also with `-C user=deploy,host=ci,addr=192.0.2.10`) and visudo checks sudoers files.
mission.objective: Make image/ satisfy every point of CHECKLIST.md without breaking any of the others: points that are already compliant must stay compliant, files must not be deleted to make a point pass (the checklist says what has to stay), and sshd must stay valid with all its other settings unchanged. The check reports only the number of the first point that fails.

mission.name: Reading the Sick Box
mission.description: On-call pasted `top -b -n1` from the sick database host into top.txt before rebooting it. The incident report needs five numbers from that paste, and the template summary.env is waiting to be filled in.
mission.objective: Fill in summary.env from top.txt: LOAD1 and LOAD15 (the 1-minute and 15-minute load averages), IOWAIT (the %wa figure, number only), ZOMBIES (how many zombie tasks) and TOP_MEM_PID (the PID of the process with the largest resident memory, RES).

mission.name: Who Is Eating the RAM
mission.description: The box is swapping. Five worker processes from the job runner are alive in the sandbox, next to other processes, and you need to know which three hold the most memory in RAM before anyone restarts anything.
mission.objective: Write the PIDs of the three workers (the processes running opt/workers/worker.py) with the largest resident memory (RSS) to top_rss.txt, one per line, largest first. Do not stop or signal any process.

mission.name: Out of Memory? Check Again
mission.description: A developer opened ticket MEM-7741: "server out of memory, under 200 MB free!" and pasted free -m twice, ten minutes apart, plus /proc/meminfo from the second moment. Before anyone buys RAM or restarts the service, someone has to read those numbers properly.
mission.objective: Following the rule in TICKET.md, fill memory.env from the later capture: available_mib (MiB the system can still hand out), swap_used_mib (swap in use) and verdict (ok or pressure).

mission.name: One Hour of vmstat, Sixty Samples
mission.description: During the incident someone ran `vmstat 1 60` on the app server and saved it as vmstat.txt. The post-mortem needs to know when swapping started and for how long the disks kept the CPUs waiting.
mission.objective: Following TICKET.md, write answers.env with FIRST_SWAP_SAMPLE (the number of the first sample in which memory was being swapped in or out) and HIGH_IOWAIT_SAMPLES (how many samples had iowait above 30).

mission.name: iostat by Hand
mission.description: The storage team wants to know which disk is taking the writes, but the host has no iostat history. What iostat prints comes from /proc/diskstats, and two snapshots of it, taken ten seconds apart, were saved as diskstats.1 and diskstats.2.
mission.objective: Following TICKET.md, write busiest.txt with one line: the name of the whole disk that wrote the most during the ten seconds, a space, and its average write rate in KiB/s (a whole number, within 1 of the exact value).

mission.name: Load Per CPU
mission.description: Monitoring pasted the `uptime` line of eight hosts into uptime.txt, and the CMDB export in inventory.tsv has the CPU count (nproc) of each. A load of 8 is a disaster on 2 CPUs and perfectly fine on 16, so raw numbers are no use.
mission.objective: Write the names of the hosts whose 5-minute load average per CPU is above 1.0 to overloaded.txt, one per line (hosts at exactly 1.0 are not above it).

mission.name: Policy Audit: Who Is Not Nice Enough
mission.description: Policy OPS-12 says every batch worker must run at niceness 10 or higher so the API stays responsive. After a week of hand-started jobs nobody knows which workers comply. The workers are running now, next to the API and a monitoring agent.
mission.objective: Audit the running processes and write the PIDs of the batch workers (the processes running opt/jobs/batch-*.sh) whose niceness is below 10 to violators.txt, one per line. Do not change any process.

mission.name: Make the Batch Jobs Nicer
mission.description: The audit found batch workers running below niceness 10 (policy OPS-12). They must not be stopped, because they are halfway through the nightly run, but they have to stop competing with the API. One of them is a small pipeline of three processes.
mission.objective: Without restarting anything, give every batch worker (processes running opt/jobs/batch-*.sh) that is below niceness 10 niceness 15, including every process of the batch-etl pipeline. The API, the monitoring agent and the workers that already comply must keep their current niceness exactly (a worker already at 17 or 18 must not drop to 15).
concepts: raising niceness as a normal user

mission.name: The Backup That Ate the Disk
mission.description: A colleague started a tar backup of srv/data by hand during business hours, and the database's disk latency has gone through the roof. The backup is 70% done and must not be stopped, but it must stop starving the database.
mission.objective: Without stopping or killing anything, put the running backup into the idle I/O scheduling class: the tar process and the gzip compressor that runs below it. The database process (opt/db/dbserver.sh) must keep the I/O class it has.

mission.name: The Health Check That Cries Wolf
mission.description: Every minute healthcheck.sh pages the on-call with "queue-worker DOWN", yet the queue is draining and the worker is plainly running. Someone also left a backup copy of the worker running next to the real one, and it must not fool the check.
mission.objective: Fix healthcheck.sh so that it exits 0 (printing a line with OK) while the queue worker (opt/queue-worker.sh) runs and exits 1 (printing DOWN) when it does not. A running copy named queue-worker.bak must not count as the worker. Keep the script's name, its location and the OK/DOWN lines.
concepts: how scripts appear in the process table

mission.name: Twelve Workers, Two Supervisors
mission.description: Twelve queue workers run under two supervisors, A and B. Ops has to restart exactly the e-mail workers of supervisor B (a config change for B only), and wants the list of their PIDs first.
mission.objective: Write the PIDs of the workers that consume the queue named exactly emails and are children of supervisor B (supervisor.sh B) to emails_b.txt, one per line. Workers of other queues (including emails-archive) and e-mail workers of supervisor A must not be in it.

mission.name: Put Down the Stuck Reports
mission.description: The report runner has twelve workers, report-1 to report-12, each touching a heartbeat file in run/hb/ every few seconds. Three of them hung: their heartbeat is older than two minutes. They are blocking the report queue and have to be shut down cleanly (the workers flush state when they get SIGTERM), without disturbing the nine healthy workers or the supervisor.
mission.objective: Terminate exactly the workers whose heartbeat file in run/hb/ is older than 2 minutes, with the default (graceful) signal, so that each logs its clean-shutdown line in log/workers.log. Every healthy worker and the report supervisor must still be running afterwards.

mission.name: Device or Resource Busy
mission.description: Ops wants to take the data/ volume offline for maintenance, but the unmount (and even a plain rm -r of data/) is refused with "device or resource busy". Something on this host still has the volume in use, and nobody knows what. lsof is not installed on the maintenance box, but /proc and fuser are.
mission.objective: Find every live process that uses data/ in any way: it has a file below data/ open, or data/ (or a directory inside it) is its current working directory. Write one line per process to holders.txt in the form `PID PATH`, where PATH is the open file or the directory it holds, as absolute path. Do not stop any process.

mission.name: Up, But Not Answering
mission.description: Users report connection timeouts against one of four local services, yet all four processes are running and all four ports are open. The service that times out is the one that has stopped calling accept(): its queue of waiting connections is full and new clients are being ignored.
mission.objective: Find the TCP port of the one listening service whose accept queue is full, and write just that port number to port.txt.
concepts: Recv-Q and Send-Q on LISTEN sockets

mission.name: Retiring netstat
mission.description: The old monitoring plugin conn_states.sh counts TCP connections per state with `netstat -tan`. The net-tools package is being removed from every host next week, and the plugin's output feeds dashboards and alert rules that match on exact state names, so nothing about the output may change.
mission.objective: Rewrite conn_states.sh (in place) to use ss instead of netstat, so that its output is byte-for-byte what the old script printed: one `STATE count` line per state, sorted, with netstat's state names. The script must not call netstat any more.

mission.name: Full Disk, Free Space
mission.description: The mail host refuses to create files: "No space left on device", yet `df -h` shows 40 % free everywhere. The on-call engineer saved the output of `df -h` and `df -i` in captured/, and rsynced the suspect filesystem's tree to spool/ in the sandbox so it can be examined safely.
mission.objective: Find the filesystem that is really full (see captured/) and the one directory inside the local spool/ tree that holds the most files directly. Write one line to culprit.txt: the mount point, a space, and the directory path (relative to the sandbox, for example `spool/mail/x`).

mission.name: Where Did the Disk Go
mission.description: Disk usage on the application host jumped overnight and the capacity alert wants to know where. A copy of the host's var/ tree is in the sandbox, including a large VM disk image and a set of backup snapshots that share files with each other.
mission.objective: Write top5.txt: the five directories exactly two levels below var/ (like var/lib/x) that use the most real disk space, biggest first, one path per line. A du output with sizes in front of the paths is fine. Hidden directories count.

mission.name: The Minute It Broke
mission.description: The last hour of the application host's journal was exported with `journalctl -o json` into journal.json (one JSON object per line). Somewhere in that hour the error rate jumped, and the incident report needs the exact minute and the service that was producing most of the errors then.
mission.objective: Find the first minute (UTC) in which more than 10 error-level entries were logged, and the systemd unit that logged the most errors in that minute. Write them to spike.txt as one line: `HH:MM unit` (for example `09:41 foo.service`). Errors are entries with a syslog priority of 3 (err) or more severe.

mission.name: Turn Down the Noise
mission.description: app.log grows by 2 GB a day and the log shipper bill shows it. Most of the volume is three chatty messages that nobody reads, but the log also contains real ERROR lines that must never be dropped, and some of them look suspiciously like the noise.
mission.objective: Find the three message templates that produce the most lines, once numbers, IDs and IP addresses are ignored. Write a file drop.patterns, one extended regex per line, so that `grep -vEf drop.patterns app.log` removes every line of those three templates and nothing else: every other line, ERROR lines above all, must survive.
concepts: regex anchoring on the log level

mission.name: 100 Percent of Nothing
mission.description: The monitoring graph shows the CPUs pinned at 100 %, but `top` never shows a single process above a few percent. Something is burning CPU in tiny, short-lived pieces: each piece is gone before you can look at it, and the next one has a different PID. Two other loops on the host also spawn short-lived children all the time, but theirs are harmless.
mission.objective: Find the long-running parent process that keeps spawning the CPU-heavy short-lived children and write its PID (just the number) to culprit.txt. Do not kill anything.

mission.name: The Slow Leak
mission.description: Memory use on the app host has been creeping up for days. Four worker processes of the same service are running, and when memory runs out the OOM killer will pick a victim on its own, probably the wrong one. One of the workers leaks; the others are fine, even though one of them is much bigger than the rest.
mission.objective: Identify the leaking worker and measure how fast it grows. Write one line to leak.txt: its PID, a space, and its growth rate in KiB per second as a whole number (for example `4242 87`). The rate must be within 20 % of the real one, so measure over at least 10 seconds. Do not kill anything.

mission.name: Too Many Open Files
mission.description: The API intermittently logs "Too many open files" and drops requests. Four services run on this host and each has its own file descriptor limit. One of them is leaking descriptors and is about to hit its limit, but it is not the one with the most descriptors open.
mission.objective: Find the process that is close to its open-file limit and write fdleak.env with four lines: `pid=` its PID, `type=` the kind of descriptor it leaks (socket, pipe or file), `limit=` its current soft limit on open files, and `fds=` how many descriptors it has open now (within 5 of the real count). Do not kill anything.

mission.name: One Sample per Second
mission.description: Capacity planning wants a CSV of how one process behaves over time, and they want to collect it with a script you write, not with a monitoring suite. The process to watch is the nightly ETL job, whose name contains spaces and parentheses, which is exactly the kind of detail that breaks naive parsing of /proc.
mission.objective: Write sample.sh in the sandbox so that `bash sample.sh PID N` prints N lines `epoch,rss_kib,cpu_ticks`, one per second, for the process PID: the Unix time, its resident memory in KiB, and its CPU time in clock ticks (user plus system). No header line. If the process disappears while sampling, the script must stop quietly and exit with status 0, printing nothing broken.
concepts: comm field with spaces and parentheses
robust exit when the PID vanishes

mission.name: Everything Is Slow
mission.description: Tickets keep coming in: "everything is slow". On this host four different things are going wrong at once: a scheduler that spawns CPU-heavy jobs all day, a worker whose memory keeps growing, a service that stopped accepting connections, and a debug logger that fills the disk and is restarted by a supervisor whenever it dies. Next to them run a healthy API server (big, but fine) and an audit logger that must not be disturbed.
mission.objective: 1) Write triage.env with the culprit of each problem as KEY=value lines: SPAWNER_PID (the long-running parent that spawns the CPU-heavy short-lived children), LEAKER_PID, LEAKER_RSS_KIB (its resident memory in KiB at the time you looked, within 5 %), STUCK_PORT (the listening port whose accept queue is full) and LOGWRITER_PID (the process writing the runaway log, or its supervisor). 2) Then mitigate: renice the spawner to 19 and leave it running; stop the leaker; stop the log writer for good (it must not come back). Leave the healthy API server, the audit logger and the stuck service alone.
concepts: fuser / open files of a runaway writer
recording evidence before stopping a process

mission.name: The Invisible Key
mission.description: The report service refuses to start: "app.conf: invalid key 'port'". The line looks perfect on screen, so something in the file is not what it seems.
mission.objective: Clean app.conf in place so that it contains only plain text: Unix line endings, no trailing whitespace on any line, and no non-breaking spaces. Keep every setting and comment, and keep the layout `key = value` like the other lines.

mission.name: Which Upload Limit?
mission.description: Support ticket 4471: customers get "413 Request Entity Too Large" on uploads.example.com. The reverse proxy config nginx-full.conf was generated from 80 vhosts and is about 6000 lines long.
mission.objective: Find the client_max_body_size that applies to the whole uploads.example.com virtual host (the value set directly in its server block, not inside a location) and write just that value, for example 10m, to answer.txt. Do not edit nginx-full.conf.

mission.name: Staging Moves Over
mission.description: Ports 8080 are crowded on the staging box, so the team agreed that staging moves to 9080. services.conf also holds production, which must stay on 8080, and several comments that mention the old port.
mission.objective: Change the port of the [staging] section of services.conf from 8080 to 9080, editing the file in place and keeping the original as services.conf.bak. Production, the other sections and every comment must stay exactly as they were.

mission.name: Drain Rack B
mission.description: Facilities will cut power to rack B on Friday. The load balancer reads upstreams.tab, a hand-aligned table of backends, and traffic must stop going to every rack-B host before then.
mission.objective: In upstreams.tab set the weight of every backend that is in rack B to 0, without touching other rows. The file's column alignment and all comment and blank lines must stay exactly as they are (only the weight column of rack-B rows changes).

mission.name: Names Without Secrets
mission.description: Security is auditing prod.env. They want the list of variable names (never the values) and proof that a teammate's script did not truncate the base64 signing key when it rewrote the file last week.
mission.objective: Write keys.txt with the name of every variable defined in prod.env, one per line, in file order, without values, comments, blank lines or the 'export ' prefix. Write signing_key.txt with the complete value of SIGNING_KEY, including any trailing '=' characters. Do not modify prod.env.

mission.name: One Line for the Balancer
mission.description: The load balancer reads its backend list from a single BACKENDS= line in lb.env. The backends are kept in two parallel lists, hosts.txt and ports.txt, and someone must combine them.
mission.objective: Append one line to lb.env of the form BACKENDS=host1:port1,host2:port2,... built from hosts.txt and ports.txt (the first host with the first port, and so on, in order). Keep all existing lines of lb.env; the BACKENDS line must be the last one and there must be exactly one.

mission.name: One Site per File
mission.description: The monolithic sites.conf holds seven nginx server blocks. The new deployment tool wants one file per site in sites-available/, named after the site, and the header comment kept in its own file.
mission.objective: Create the directory sites-available/ and split sites.conf into it: one file per server block named <first server_name>.conf (for example shop.example.com.conf), plus 00-header.conf holding the comment lines at the top. Each file must contain its block exactly as written (nested blocks included). Leave sites.conf in place.

mission.name: Reformatted and Tweaked
mission.description: A teammate's pull request is titled "reformat haproxy.cfg and small tweaks". The old file is haproxy.orig.cfg and the new one haproxy.cfg. A plain diff shows hundreds of changed lines because the indentation was rewritten.
mission.objective: Write changed.txt listing the directives whose value really changed between haproxy.orig.cfg and haproxy.cfg, one directive name per line (for example 'timeout'), ignoring re-indentation, extra spaces and blank lines. Do not modify either haproxy file.

mission.name: Half a Vendor Patch
mission.description: The proxy vendor shipped fix-timeouts.patch against their stock proxy.conf. Our copy has local tuning, so the patch does not go in cleanly: one change is rejected.
mission.objective: Apply fix-timeouts.patch to proxy.conf so that all three of the vendor's timeout changes are in the file and all of our local edits are still there. Finish the rejected change by hand. When you are done there must be no .rej or .orig files left in the directory.

mission.name: Fill the Template, Spare nginx
mission.description: The deployment renders nginx.conf from nginx.conf.tmpl. Two placeholders, $APP_HOST and $APP_PORT, belong to the deployment (their values are in deploy.env). The template also contains nginx's own variables, which nginx fills in at request time.
mission.objective: Render nginx.conf from nginx.conf.tmpl: replace $APP_HOST and ${APP_PORT} with the values from deploy.env, and leave every nginx variable ($host, $remote_addr, $request_uri, $http_upgrade, $scheme, ...) exactly as it is in the template.

mission.name: One Config per Environment
mission.description: Every environment gets its own app config, generated from app.conf.tmpl and one row of envs.csv. The values of prod and dr contain characters that are special to sed.
mission.objective: Create the directory out/ and generate out/dev.conf, out/staging.conf, out/prod.conf and out/dr.conf: each is app.conf.tmpl with the {{ENV}}, {{DB_URL}}, {{DB_PASSWORD}} and {{REPLICAS}} placeholders replaced by that environment's values from envs.csv (skip the header row). Values must appear literally, exactly as written in the CSV.

mission.name: Tune the Database Section
mission.description: A DBA ticket for my.cnf: the database needs more connections and a bigger buffer pool. Several sections of the file have settings with similar names, and the [mysqld] section appears twice (that is legal; MySQL merges the blocks).
mission.objective: In my.cnf set max_connections to 500 and add innodb_buffer_pool_size = 2G, both in the first [mysqld] block. Change nothing else: [client] and [mysqldump] keep their own max_allowed_packet lines, and every comment, setting and the order of the file must stay as it is.

mission.name: Compose After the Hotfix
mission.description: A late-night hotfix left compose.yml unparsable, so the stack will not come up, and the release that is going out tonight needs a new worker image.
mission.objective: Repair compose.yml so that it parses as YAML, and bump only the worker service's image to tag 2.7.1. The api service stays on 2.7.0, and every other key, value and comment must stay exactly as it is.

mission.name: Flag Day
mission.description: The checkout team is rolling out the new checkout in Europe, and the flags file in the repo has to follow before the deploy.
mission.objective: Edit flags.json: enable new_checkout for the eu region only, add "beta-12" to the testers array, and delete the expired xmas_banner flag. Everything else, including the key order, must stay as it is, and the file must remain valid JSON.

mission.name: Hosts Before the DNS Move
mission.description: Before the DNS migration the shared etc/hosts must be cleaned up. Years of copy-paste left duplicates, hosts spread over several lines per address, and machines that no longer exist.
mission.objective: Clean etc/hosts: remove duplicate entries, put every IP address on exactly one line with all of its names, and comment out (do not delete) the decommissioned 10.9.* hosts. The localhost and IPv6 lines stay untouched and first, every comment stays, and every name must still resolve to the address it resolves to today (the resolver uses the first matching line).

mission.name: Resolver That Remembers
mission.description: Ticket NET-212: this host should use the two new DNS servers and search corp.example first. Someone edited etc/resolv.conf and it worked, until the next restart wiped it. The host runs systemd-resolved (a small stand-in is in bin/: systemctl and resolvectl).
mission.objective: Configure systemd-resolved the way it expects (a drop-in under etc/systemd/resolved.conf.d/) so that DNS servers are exactly 10.20.0.53 then 10.20.0.54, and the search domains are corp.example then lab.example. Restart systemd-resolved with the mock systemctl so it takes effect. etc/resolv.conf must still be the symlink to the stub file, and etc/systemd/resolved.conf (the package's file) stays unchanged.

mission.name: Hop Through the Bastion
mission.description: The six db-* servers are only reachable through bastion.corp, and each one has its own login user and key. The current home/.ssh/config was started by a colleague and does not work for anything.
mission.objective: Rewrite home/.ssh/config so that `ssh db-N` works for every host listed in db-hosts.txt (right user, port and key, reached through bastion.corp as the jump host, real name db-N.corp.internal), bastion.corp itself uses user jump with key keys/bastion, github.com uses user git with keys/github and no jump host, gitlab.corp keeps its existing settings, and every other host gets only safe defaults: ServerAliveInterval 30, no agent forwarding, and no forced User.

mission.name: One Drop-in, Once in PATH
mission.description: The vendor tool lives in opt/tool/bin and every login shell on the fleet should find it. A colleague left a draft in etc/profile.d that nothing ever loads.
mission.objective: Write etc/profile.d/tool.sh so that, for sh and for bash, the directory $SANDBOX/opt/tool/bin ends up in PATH exactly once even if the profile is sourced several times or the directory is already in PATH, and only if the directory exists. PATH must not change when the directory is missing, other profile.d scripts must keep working, and the script must run under a plain POSIX sh (dash) without errors.

mission.name: Mail That Goes Nowhere
mission.description: Cron mail for root vanishes because root is aliased to a mailbox of an engineer who left in September. Ticket MAIL-77 asks for a proper routing, and the departed engineer's address has to go from every list.
mission.objective: Update etc/aliases: root goes to the on-call list (etc/oncall.list, as an :include: of its full path), add the alias security delivering to secops@corp.example and soc-oncall@corp.example, and remove mkhan@corp.example (any capitalisation) everywhere, in etc/aliases and in etc/oncall.list. An alias that would be left without any recipient is removed; colleagues whose names merely start with mkhan stay. Then rebuild the database with newaliases without any warning. All other aliases and comments stay.

mission.name: Who Can Write to Builds
mission.description: The security scanner reports that /srv/builds on the file server is writable by the whole world, and that the ISO mirror allows root on clients to act as root on the server. A stand-in exportfs is in bin/ (it works on etc/exports of this sandbox).
mission.objective: Fix etc/exports: /srv/builds is exported read-write to the subnet 10.20.0.0/24 and to nobody else, /srv/iso is exported read-only to everyone, and no_root_squash appears nowhere. Keep the /srv/backup entry and the comments as they are, and apply the change with exportfs -r so that exportfs -v shows the new state.

mission.name: A Prompt That Tells the Truth
mission.description: Ops wants a prompt that shows where you are and whether the last command failed. The current one in home/.bashrc was copied from a blog: it is colourful, but long commands wrap over their own prompt line.
mission.objective: Change the prompt in home/.bashrc so that it shows user@host:directory (with ~ for the home directory) and the prompt character, adds the exit code of the last command in red only when it is not zero, and wraps every colour escape sequence for readline (\[ and \]). Keep the aliases, EDITOR and history settings of the file.

mission.name: Rescue Box Editing
mission.description: On a rescue box only vi is installed, and squid.conf (400 lines) needs five precise changes before the proxy can come back. The list is in CHANGES.txt.
mission.objective: Make the five changes listed in CHANGES.txt to squid.conf, and nothing else. The line numbers in the list refer to the file as it is now. Any editor is accepted (edit, nano, sed or vi); the result must match the expected file exactly.

mission.name: A Year of Hand Edits
mission.description: A web server was hand-edited for a year. The golden configuration is in golden/etc/, the server's live copy in live/etc/, and allowed-overrides.txt lists the local differences that are permitted. The audit wants a report and a clean server.
mission.objective: Write drift.txt with one path per line (relative to etc/, for example ssh/sshd_config) for exactly the files that drifted: changed content, changed mode only, missing from live, and extra files in live that are not allowed. Then restore everything: drifted files get golden's content and mode (but an allowed override line must survive inside a file that also drifted elsewhere), missing files are restored, and unallowed extra files are moved into quarantine/ instead of being deleted. Afterwards diff -r golden/etc live/etc may only show the allowed overrides, and modes must match golden.

mission.name: Migration Aftermath
mission.description: The app will not start after the config migration to the 4.x format. Its --check-config option stops at the first error it finds, and the configuration is spread over five files in five formats. MIGRATION.txt lists what the final values have to be.
mission.objective: Repair the five files in etc/app/ (app.ini, app.env, features.json, services.yml, hosts) until bin/app --check-config reports no error, with every value as listed in MIGRATION.txt (do not make errors disappear by deleting the setting). Then start the app with bin/app start: it must answer on its port, and curl on 127.0.0.1 must return the version string from MIGRATION.txt.

mission.name: Which Leg Is the Database?
mission.description: The billing app on app-07 must bind to the host's own address in the database subnet 10.20.0.0/22, or the DB firewall drops its connections. Nobody remembers which interface that is; TICKET.txt has the details and ip-addr.txt is `ip addr` from the host.
mission.objective: Write db-iface.env with three lines: IFACE=<the interface the address in 10.20.0.0/22 is configured on>, ADDR=<that address without the /prefix> and STATE=<that interface's state as ip prints it>.

mission.name: Which Way Out?

mission.description: The ops crontab runs three helpers as ./bin/<name>. Every one of them works when you type `bash bin/disk_report data/df.txt` or `python3 bin/queue_stats data/queue.txt`, yet cron keeps mailing errors (cron-mail.txt) and none of them has produced a report in weeks.
mission.objective: Fix bin/disk_report, bin/queue_stats and bin/backup_age so that each one runs correctly when started directly as ./bin/<name> FILE, the way cron starts it (see crontab.txt), without printing any error. Keep what the programs do; they are tested on data you have not seen.

mission.name: Green Dashboard
mission.description: The monitoring dashboard has shown all four mail queues as healthy for a week, while mx3 had almost 2000 stuck messages and mx4 stopped writing stats altogether. Monitoring only looks at the exit status of check_queue.sh (monitoring.log).
mission.objective: Fix check_queue.sh so that `./check_queue.sh STATS_FILE` prints exactly one line and exits with the code its header asks for: 0 OK, 1 WARNING, 2 CRITICAL, and 3 UNKNOWN (with the line `UNKNOWN - no queue data in STATS_FILE`) when the file is missing, unreadable or has no numeric deferred= value. It is tested with stats files you have not seen.
concepts: $? is the status of the last command

mission.name: Lost in Transit
mission.description: The month-end job calls archive.sh to store finance reports in the object store. Files with spaces in their names arrive as several broken uploads or not at all (TICKET.txt), and a call without arguments silently succeeds.
mission.objective: Fix archive.sh so that `./archive.sh BUCKET FILE...` calls `./tools/upload --bucket BUCKET FILE...` once, passing BUCKET and every FILE as exactly the argument it received (spaces, empty strings and characters like * included), and keeps printing `archiving N file(s) to BUCKET` first. With fewer than 2 arguments it must print a usage line to stderr, exit 2 and upload nothing. upload.log shows how upload was called.

mission.name: Option Parsing
mission.description: Ops wants to run rotate.sh from cron with options like `-vn3 -d /var/log/worker 'worker-*.log'` (crontab.txt). The rotation code at the bottom of the script works; the part that reads the options was never written.
mission.objective: Add option parsing to rotate.sh as its header describes: -n COUNT (default 7), -d DIR (required), -v, in any order, clustered (-vn3) or with attached values (-dlogs), with everything after the options (or after --) left in "$@" as patterns. An unknown option, an option missing its value, or no -d must print the usage line on stderr and exit 2 before anything is deleted. It is tested with many command lines on fresh directories.

mission.name: Return to Sender
mission.description: The upload scripts share lib/units.sh. Since someone added to_bytes, `./check_upload.sh 64K uploads/*` never reports anything as too big, and a script that sources the library found its own $size variable changed behind its back (NOTES.txt).
mission.objective: Fix to_bytes in lib/units.sh so that, as its comment says, it prints the size in bytes on stdout and returns 0, prints nothing and returns 1 for anything that is not a whole number with an optional K, M, G or T, and creates or changes no variable in the shell that calls it. check_upload.sh must then work unchanged. It is tested by sourcing the library and calling to_bytes with many inputs.

mission.name: Batch Job
mission.description: upload_batch.sh sends the files listed in manifest.txt to the media store, four per request. Since the marketing team started using real file names, "Q3 report.pdf" arrives as two missing files called "media/Q3" and "report.pdf", and the upload count is wrong.
mission.objective: Fix upload_batch.sh so that `./upload_batch.sh MANIFEST` passes every non-empty line of MANIFEST to ./tools/upload as exactly one argument (spaces, double spaces, backslashes and glob characters kept), in manifest order and in calls of at most 4 files, and then prints `uploaded N files` with the right N. upload.log records every call. It is tested with manifests you have not seen.

mission.name: Gaps in the Dumps
mission.description: The DBA needs to know which nightly database dumps are missing (REQUEST.txt). Some nights the backup job left no file, some nights a 0-byte one, and the ranges people ask about keep crossing the end of a month.
mission.objective: Write missing_backups.sh as its header describes: `./missing_backups.sh START END` prints, in order, every day from START to END (both included) whose backups/db-YYYY-MM-DD.sql.gz is missing or empty, and exits 1 if it printed any day, 0 if none. Not exactly 2 arguments, a date that does not exist, or END before START: a message on stderr, nothing on stdout, exit 2. It is tested on other backup directories and ranges across month and year ends.

mission.name: Roll Call
mission.description: check_hosts.sh is supposed to log in to every host in inventory.txt and record its uptime, but status.txt only ever contains web-01. ./tools/remote is this lab's stand-in for ssh and behaves like it, and the inventory comes straight from the CMDB export.
mission.objective: Fix check_hosts.sh so that `./check_hosts.sh INVENTORY` calls ./tools/remote once for every host in INVENTORY, in order, and writes status.txt as its header describes (`host: output` or `host: UNREACHABLE`, one line per host, no stray characters). Skip comments and empty lines, cope with Windows line endings, and include the last host even when the file does not end with a newline. It is tested with another inventory as well.
concepts: commands that read stdin inside a loop

mission.name: Preflight
mission.description: The pipeline runs `./preflight.sh && ./deploy.sh`, and preflight.sh has not stopped a single deploy in months: not with 60 MB free on /srv, not during a change freeze, not for a feature branch without FORCE=1 (INCIDENT.txt). Meanwhile a mysterious file called 500 keeps appearing.
mission.objective: Fix the four checks in preflight.sh so that it does exactly what its header says for any combination of inputs: the first failing check prints its STOP line and exits 1 (config missing or empty, less than 500 MB free, TODAY inside a freeze window with both days included, a branch other than main without FORCE=1), otherwise it prints `GO: deploying BRANCH` and exits 0. Always exactly one line, and no stray files. It is tested in many scenarios through the environment variables.

mission.name: Special Delivery
mission.description: The vendor drops archives into inbox/ and the import job runs unpack.sh on each one. Tarballs come out as a bare .tar file and the original disappears, the .ZIP deliveries are "unknown", and an unsupported .rar is reported as a success (SUPPORT.txt).
mission.objective: Fix unpack.sh so that it follows its header for every file type: .tar.gz, .tgz, .tar.xz and .zip (in any letter case) extract into a directory NAME/ in the current directory, a plain .gz becomes the file NAME, the original file is never changed or removed, and anything else prints a message on stderr, creates nothing and exits 2. It is tested with other archives, from a different working directory.

mission.name: Make Believe
mission.description: The build wrapper asks needs_rebuild.sh whether each target is stale. Every CI run recompiles everything, because the cached build output has the same timestamps as the checkout, and last week a deleted header made it answer "up to date" instead of failing (CI-NOTES.txt).
mission.objective: Fix needs_rebuild.sh so that `./needs_rebuild.sh TARGET SRC...` answers exactly as its header says, only through its exit status: 0 when TARGET is missing (a dangling symlink counts as missing) or a SRC is newer, 1 when it is up to date (equal times included), 2 with the given stderr message when there are too few arguments or a SRC is missing, a broken symlink or unreadable. It is tested with many timestamp combinations.

mission.name: Name Tag
mission.description: The release bot needs the app name, version, OS, architecture and extension of every file it publishes. parse_artifact.sh gets them wrong for any app with a hyphen in its name, and on the bot's minimal runner it cannot even start cut, sed or basename (RUNNER.txt).
mission.objective: Rewrite parse_artifact.sh so that `./parse_artifact.sh FILE` prints `name=... version=... os=... arch=... ext=...` for every name in the format its header describes (a leading directory ignored), and for anything else prints `parse_artifact: not an artifact name: FILE` on stderr and exits 1. It must work with bash alone: it is tested as `env -i PATH=/nonexistent /bin/bash parse_artifact.sh NAME` with names you have not seen.

mission.name: Quota Report
mission.description: The weekly disk quota mail comes from quota_report.sh. This week it printed `division by 0` and `value too great for base` errors and warned nobody. The storage export (usage.tsv) pads every size with zeros to 8 digits; NOTE.txt describes the format.
mission.objective: Fix quota_report.sh so that `bash quota_report.sh FILE` prints, in file order, `<user> <percent>%` for every user using at least 90 % of their quota (percent = used * 100 / quota, rounded down; a quota of 0 means unlimited and is never listed), then `TOTAL <n> MiB`, where n is all used KiB added up and divided by 1024, rounded down. Nothing else on stdout, no errors on stderr. It is also run on an export you have not seen.

mission.name: Tag Without a Hash
mission.description: Release 1.2.0 shipped tagged `app-1.2.0--20261110`: the CI runner had lost its .git directory, git failed, and make_tag.sh still exited 0 and wrote release.tag. INCIDENT.txt shows how to replay it with the stand-in bin/git.
mission.objective: Fix make_tag.sh so that, run in the checkout as `PATH="$PWD/bin:$PATH" ./make_tag.sh`, it writes release.tag with exactly one line `app-<version>-<sha>-<date>`: version from VERSION (no CR or newline), sha from `git rev-parse --short HEAD`, date from $TAG_DATE or else today as YYYYMMDD. When git fails, or VERSION is missing or empty, it must exit non-zero with a message on stderr and leave release.tag as it was (or absent).

mission.name: Stale Accounts
mission.description: The quarterly access audit runs stale_accounts.sh to find server accounts whose owners have left. It prints TOTAL 0 every time, it lists root and daemon, and on the audit runner it dies because it cannot create temp files. AUDIT.txt has the rules.
mission.objective: Fix stale_accounts.sh so that `bash stale_accounts.sh USERS_EXPORT HR_ROSTER` prints, sorted, one per line, every human account (uid 1000 to 59999) whose login HR does not list as active or leave (HR writes logins in capitals), then `TOTAL n`. It runs in a read-only directory with an unwritable TMPDIR, so it may not create any file: use process substitution `<( )` instead of temp files. It is also run on a second export and roster.

mission.name: Two Kinds of Dollar
mission.description: gen_vhost.sh creates the nginx vhost and a health check script for every new site. Since the last edit, the vhosts come out with empty `$host` headers and the health checks contain `$domain` instead of the site name. examples/ shows the right output for `./gen_vhost.sh shop.example.com 8081`.
mission.objective: Fix gen_vhost.sh so that `./gen_vhost.sh DOMAIN PORT` writes sites/DOMAIN.conf and an executable sites/DOMAIN-healthcheck.sh that are identical to the two files in examples/ with shop.example.com and 8081 replaced by DOMAIN and PORT: nginx's own variables and the generated script's $1, $path and $url stay literal. With a missing argument or a PORT that is not a number it must print usage on stderr, exit 2 and write nothing. It is tested with domains you have not seen.

mission.name: Leftover Lock
mission.description: Last night the scheduler killed nightly_export.sh with SIGTERM when it overran. It left export.lock and a temp directory behind, so tonight's run refused to start. On Tuesday the converter failed halfway and the BI team loaded a half-written export.csv. ONCALL.txt has the log and how to replay it.
mission.objective: Fix nightly_export.sh so that after every run (success, a failing to_csv, or SIGTERM in the middle of the slow fetch) export.lock and its temp directory (under $TMPDIR, as mktemp -d makes it) are gone and export.csv is either the complete new export or yesterday's file, untouched. A failure must exit non-zero; SIGTERM must make it exit with status 143 within 3 seconds and stop the fetch step it started. When export.lock already exists, it must exit non-zero and leave that lock alone.
concepts: traps wait for the foreground command

mission.name: Set -e Was On
mission.description: deploy.sh starts with `set -e`, yet last night the database migration failed and the script carried on and put the release live anyway. POSTMORTEM.txt shows how to replay it: the stand-in bin/step logs every step to steps.log and fails the one named in FAIL_STEP.
mission.objective: Fix deploy.sh so that whichever step fails (fetch, build, migrate, schema-version or verify), it stops right after that step: no later step runs (above all not deploy) and it exits with a non-zero status. With no failing step it must still run fetch, build, migrate, schema-version, verify and deploy in that order and exit 0.

mission.name: Typo in rm
mission.description: clean_build.sh empties a project's build/ folder before every CI build. Last night it deleted all of workspace/shop, sources included, and when a job forgot to set PROJECT it deleted every project (INCIDENT.txt). Running the draft really deletes files here; type reset to get them back.
mission.objective: Harden clean_build.sh: turn on `set -u` so an unset variable stops it, and find the bug. With PROJECT unset or empty it must exit non-zero and delete nothing. `PROJECT=NAME ./clean_build.sh` must empty workspace/NAME/build (keeping the folder) and touch nothing else, also when no TARGET argument and no DEBUG are given; `PROJECT=NAME ./clean_build.sh TARGET` removes only build/TARGET; DEBUG=1 adds messages on stderr. It is tested on a workspace you have not seen.

mission.name: 20-Byte Backups
mission.description: At Monday's restore drill, the last nine nightly backups turned out to be 20-byte empty archives, although every night backup_db.sh reported `backup ok`. The database host had been dropping connections and pg_dump died halfway (RESTORE_DRILL.txt; bin/pg_dump is a stand-in).
mission.objective: Fix backup_db.sh and turn on `set -o pipefail`. When pg_dump or gzip fails it must exit non-zero, leave no backups/db.sql.gz behind, and print a line starting with `backup FAILED:` on stderr that names the stage that failed (pg_dump or gzip, not both). A good dump must still exit 0 with the complete dump in backups/db.sql.gz and `backup ok: ... (N warnings)` on stdout, also on a night with 0 warnings.

mission.name: Trace the Total
mission.description: invoice_sync.sh (about 120 lines) builds the per-customer totals for accounting. E*Trade Europe disputes its statement: every other customer is right, theirs is far too high, and nobody can find why by reading the code (TICKET.txt).
mission.objective: Give invoice_sync.sh a debug mode: with DEBUG=1 it writes an xtrace to trace.log in the current directory, every line starting with the + marks, the script name and the line number (like `+./invoice_sync.sh:42: `), while stdout and stderr stay exactly as without it; without DEBUG no trace.log is created. Then use the trace to find and fix the bug: `./invoice_sync.sh [DATA_DIR]` must print the right total for every customer, also for a dataset you have not seen. Needs bash 4.1 or newer.

mission.name: One Library
mission.description: rotate_logs.sh, check_inbox.sh and sync_assets.sh in scripts/ each carry their own copy of log, die and require_cmd, and the copies have drifted: one logs to stdout, one exits 2 instead of 1. The team agreed on one shared version (STYLE.txt). Admins start the scripts by full path, from the repo, and through the links in bin/.
mission.objective: Create lib/common.sh with log, die and require_cmd exactly as STYLE.txt describes, and make the three scripts use it instead of their own copies. Each script must work when started by full path from any directory, as scripts/NAME.sh from the repo, through bin/NAME, and through another symlink to bin/NAME elsewhere. Sourcing lib/common.sh must print nothing, change no shell option or directory, never exit the caller, and a second source must change nothing.

mission.name: Prune for Everyone
mission.description: prune.sh was written in a hurry during the disk-full incident: it only works from one folder, always keeps 7, breaks on names with spaces and prints its chatter into the output that other scripts read. Now every team wants to run it from cron and from their own scripts. REQUEST.txt is the interface they agreed on.
mission.objective: Rewrite prune.sh to the interface in REQUEST.txt: `prune.sh [OPTIONS] [DIR]` deletes the *.tar.gz files directly in DIR except the N most recently modified; -k/--keep N (also --keep=N), -n/--dry-run, -h/--help, and -- are supported; settings come from defaults, then the config file ($PRUNE_CONFIG or ~/.config/prune.conf), then PRUNE_KEEP/PRUNE_DIR, then the command line, each overriding the one before. stdout holds only the deleted (or would-be-deleted) names, oldest first; everything else goes to stderr. Exit 0 when done, 1 when DIR does not exist, 2 on a usage error. A second run deletes nothing. It is tested with about 20 command lines on folders you have not seen.
concepts: stdout for data, stderr for logs

mission.name: Nightly Runner
mission.description: The nightly health checks run from cron through run_checks.sh, a first draft that runs everything in checks.d/ once. Last week a dead NFS mount made one check hang until morning, a flaky API check paged someone at 2 a.m., the README was reported as a failed check, and two overlapping runs wrote one summary over the other. SPEC.txt says how it must work.
mission.objective: Write run_checks.sh to SPEC.txt: started from its folder, it runs every executable regular file directly in checks.d/ in name order (nothing else), limits each attempt to CHECK_TIMEOUT seconds, retries a failing or timed-out check up to 3 attempts in total, waiting RETRY_DELAY seconds before the 2nd attempt and twice that before the 3rd, writes summary.txt as `<name> <PASS|FAIL|TIMEOUT> <attempts>` lines plus `failed <n> of <total>`, and exits with the number of checks that did not pass. While another run holds run_checks.lock it must exit 75 at once. It is tested with check sets you have not seen. Needs Linux (flock, timeout).

mission.name: Windows CSV Rejected
mission.description: Sales exported the address book from an old Windows CRM to contacts.csv. The new CRM's importer rejects it with 'header error: unknown column "first_name"' (although first_name is clearly the first word of the file) and stops at the first blank row. The file looks fine in cat.
mission.objective: Write contacts_clean.csv: the header and every contact row of contacts.csv, unchanged and in the same order, but with no byte-order mark before the header, every line ending in a plain LF (no carriage returns), and no empty lines. Leave contacts.csv as it is.

mission.name: Quarter From Three Months
mission.description: Finance keeps one invoice export per month: jan.csv, feb.csv and mar.csv, each starting with its own header line. The Q1 review needs them as one file, and last quarter's attempt had three header lines in it and one invoice that 'vanished'.
mission.objective: Write q1.csv: the header line once at the top, then the data rows of jan.csv, feb.csv and mar.csv, in that month order and each file's rows in their original order, every invoice on its own line. Leave the three monthly files unchanged.

mission.name: The Column Moved
mission.description: The newsletter vendor changed its export format between last quarter's old_export.csv and this quarter's new_export.csv: same subscribers' kind of data, but the columns were reordered and new ones added. Marketing wants one plain list of addresses to load into the mailing tool.
mission.objective: Write emails.txt with the value of the email column of every data row: first all rows of old_export.csv, then all rows of new_export.csv, each file in its own row order, one address per line, no header word. Use the column named exactly email in each file. Leave both exports unchanged.

mission.name: Big Refunds For Audit
mission.description: The auditors are looking at refunds this quarter. orders.csv is the shop's order export (order_id,customer,date,amount,status); the status was typed by three different systems over the years, so its spelling and case vary.
mission.objective: Write big_refunds.csv: the header line of orders.csv, then every order whose status is refunded (in any letter case) and whose amount is more than 100.00, unchanged and in the original order. Partially refunded orders do not count, and neither does an amount of exactly 100.00. Leave orders.csv unchanged.

mission.name: Hottest Readings
mission.description: The plant's data logger exports readings.csv (sensor,timestamp,value). Different sensor firmware writes numbers differently: -3.5, 12, 0.75 and scientific notation such as 1.2e3 or 4.75E2. Ops suspects a few sensors spiked and wants the worst readings first.
mission.objective: Write top10.txt with the 10 data rows of readings.csv that have the highest value (as a number: 1.2e3 is 1200), highest first, each row copied unchanged, no header. Leave readings.csv unchanged.

mission.name: First Come Within Priority
mission.description: The helpdesk tool died and the support queue survives only as queue.txt: one ticket per line (ticket id, priority P1 to P4, customer, subject), in the order the tickets arrived. The team will work through it top to bottom, and customers who wrote first must be served first within the same priority.
mission.objective: Write queue_sorted.txt: every line of queue.txt, unchanged, ordered by priority (all P1 tickets, then P2, P3, P4), and within the same priority in the order they appear in queue.txt. Leave queue.txt unchanged.

mission.name: Longest Outage
mission.description: The payment API's uptime probe runs once a minute and wrote probe.log for yesterday: a timestamp, UP or DOWN, and the latency or the error it saw. The customer's SLA is breached if a single outage lasted too long, so the total number of DOWN minutes is not the question: separate outages must not be added together.
mission.objective: Write longest_outage.txt with one line: the timestamp of the first DOWN probe of the longest unbroken run of DOWN probes, a space, and the number of probes (minutes) in that run, e.g. 2026-11-09T13:42:00Z 17. A run ends at the next UP probe, whatever errors the DOWN probes report. Leave probe.log unchanged.

mission.name: Per-Endpoint API Stats
mission.description: For Friday's API review the team wants one line of numbers per endpoint. The gateway exported yesterday's traffic as gateway.tsv: a header line, then one request per line with tab-separated time, client, method, url, status, bytes and latency_ms. URLs carry query strings (/api/users?id=7), and responses without a body (304 Not Modified) have - as their byte count.
mission.objective: Write stats.tsv, tab-separated: the header line endpoint requests bytes avg_ms max_ms, then one line per endpoint (the url without its ? and query string, so /api/users?id=7 counts as /api/users): number of requests, total bytes (- counts as 0), average latency_ms with exactly 1 decimal, and the highest latency_ms. Sort the endpoint lines by number of requests, highest first.
concepts: sub() to strip a query string

mission.name: Load Test Histogram
mission.description: Last night's load test against the checkout service ended in an incident, and the review wants to see the shape of the response times, not just an average. The JMeter results are in results.jtl, a CSV file with a header; the elapsed column is each request's total response time in milliseconds.
mission.objective: Write histogram.txt with exactly 11 lines, one per bucket of elapsed time in this order: 0-99, 100-199, 200-299, ... 900-999, then 1000+. Each line is the bucket label, a space, the number of requests in it, a space, and a bar of one # per full 10 requests (37 requests: ###; under 10: no #). A value of exactly 100 belongs to 100-199, exactly 1000 to 1000+. Buckets with no requests are listed with 0. Use the elapsed column, not Latency.
concepts: a for loop in END over every bucket
building a string in a loop

mission.name: Status Codes By Hour
mission.description: The shop's web server had a bad day: errors came in waves, and the team wants to see when. access.log is yesterday's log in the usual combined format, e.g. 203.0.113.9 - - [10/Nov/2026:14:03:22 +0000] "GET /cart HTTP/1.1" 200 5120 "-" "Mozilla/5.0 ...". The server was switched off for maintenance for a few hours at night.
mission.objective: Write status_by_hour.csv: the header line hour,2xx,3xx,4xx,5xx, then exactly 24 lines, one per hour 00 to 23 (two digits, as in the log's timestamp), each with the number of requests in that hour whose status code starts with 2, 3, 4 and 5. Hours without requests are listed with 0 in every column.

mission.name: One Timeline, Two Clocks
mission.description: A customer was charged but never got a receipt, and support needs to see what billing and notify did, in order. Both services log Unix epoch times in the first field: billing.log in seconds (1794319402), notify.log in milliseconds (1794319402518). Nobody can read either.
mission.objective: Write timeline.txt with every line of both logs, each as: the time in UTC as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ (milliseconds dropped), a space, the service name (billing or notify), a space, and the rest of the original line unchanged.
