Order the lines by time; lines in the same second keep their order: billing's lines first, then notify's, each in the order of its own log.

mission.name: Whose Third Of November
mission.description: The hotel's booking export bookings.csv has a checkin column typed by front-desk staff in three styles: 03/11/2026, 2026-11-03 and 3 Nov 2026, sometimes without leading zeros. The new channel manager accepts only ISO dates, and README.vendor explains how the numeric dates were entered.
mission.objective: Write bookings_iso.csv: bookings.csv with every checkin value rewritten as YYYY-MM-DD (two-digit month and day), read the way README.vendor describes. The header and every other column stay exactly as they are, and the rows keep their order. Leave bookings.csv unchanged.

mission.name: Bank Payroll File
mission.description: The bank sent back this month's payroll transfer file payroll.dat for reconciliation. It is a fixed-width file with no delimiters at all: every field sits at fixed columns, described in the bank's LAYOUT.txt. Finance's spreadsheet can only import CSV.
mission.objective: Write payroll.csv: the header line id,name,amount, then one line per payment (detail) record of payroll.dat, in file order. id is the employee id as written in the file (6 digits, leading zeros kept), name is the beneficiary name without the padding spaces (a name that contains a comma must be in double quotes, as CSV requires), and amount is the amount with a decimal point and two decimals, no zero padding (000012345 becomes 123.45, 000000075 becomes 0.75). Leave payroll.dat unchanged.

mission.name: Scanner Dump
mission.description: The loading dock's old handheld scanner dumps every parcel it scanned as a block of four lines (parcel id, weight in kg, postcode, dock door), with a line containing only -- between the blocks. The warehouse system wants one row per parcel, and the carrier's pickup form wants all parcel ids in one field. Some batches were synced through the Windows PC.
mission.objective: Write parcels.tsv: the header line parcel, weight_kg, postcode, dock (tab-separated), then one tab-separated row per parcel in scan_dump.txt, in dump order, with no carriage returns. Write manifest.txt: one single line with every parcel id, in dump order, separated by commas (no spaces). Leave scan_dump.txt unchanged.

mission.name: Customer Totals
mission.description: Sales wants a list of every customer with how much they ordered this year, including the customers who never ordered (the account managers want to call those). The CRM export customers.csv and the shop's orders.csv are both unsorted, both have a header line, and the customer id is in a different column in each.
mission.objective: Write customer_totals.csv: the header line customer_id,name,orders,total, then one line per customer in customers.csv, ordered by customer_id as a number (smallest first). orders is the number of orders that customer has in orders.csv and total the sum of their amounts with two decimals; a customer without orders gets 0 and 0.00. Orders whose customer_id is not in customers.csv (deleted test accounts) are not reported. Leave both input files unchanged.

mission.name: License Reconciliation
mission.description: The design tool's seats renew next week and procurement wants to know how many to buy. licenses.txt lists the seats bought (typed by hand), directory.csv is the export of all accounts with an enabled column, and active_30d.log has every SSO login event of the last 30 days. The three systems write usernames differently.
mission.objective: A user is active when their account is enabled (enabled=yes) in directory.csv and active_30d.log has at least one successful login (result=success) for them. Write unused_seats.txt with every licensed user who is not active, and unlicensed_active.txt with every active user who has no seat. Usernames in lowercase without spaces, one per line, each once, sorted. Leave the three input files unchanged.

mission.name: Orders By Region
mission.description: Every regional sales manager should get only their own region's October orders, but the shop exports one big all_orders.csv for all regions (region in column 3, rows in date order, regions mixed). Last month somebody split the file by hand; their files are still in by_region/, including one for a region that has since been merged away.
mission.objective: Fill by_region/ with exactly one file per region in all_orders.csv and nothing else. Each file is named after the region with every / replaced by - and every space by _, plus .csv (EU/West -> EU-West.csv, Asia Pacific -> Asia_Pacific.csv) and holds the header line of all_orders.csv followed by every row of that region, unchanged and in the original order. Leave all_orders.csv unchanged.
concepts: one output file per field value

mission.name: Helpdesk Export
mission.description: The helpdesk exports its tickets as tickets.csv, and every line-based tool gives a different ticket count: the notes field (in double quotes) often spans several lines, and a few subjects do too. The weekly report script is line-based and can't be changed before Friday.
mission.objective: Write tickets_flat.csv: the same CSV records as tickets.csv, header included and in the same order, but every record on exactly one line, each line break inside a field replaced by one space. Nothing else may change (fields, quotes and commas stay valid CSV). Write the number of tickets (records, not counting the header) to count.txt. Leave tickets.csv unchanged.

mission.name: Directory Export
mission.description: The nightly SSO sync rejects half of the HR export users.tsv: it says user 'u1234 ' does not exist, and 'Anna Berg' doesn't match 'Anna Berg' although they look identical. The export has padded fields, odd invisible characters, some lines saved on Windows and users that appear twice.
mission.objective: Write users_clean.tsv: users.tsv with, in every field (header included), each non-breaking space (U+00A0) turned into a normal space, every run of spaces squeezed into one, and the spaces at the start and end of the field removed. Lines end in LF only. When a username (field 1, after cleaning) appears more than once, keep only its first record. Everything else, accented letters included, stays exactly as it is. Leave users.tsv unchanged.

mission.name: Weekly Cost Mail
mission.description: Every Monday the team leads get the cloud cost per team in a plain-text mail, read in a fixed-width font. The cost export costs.csv is messy (a comment line, padding, numbers like 1e3), and last week's hand-made table was misaligned so badly that two teams were billed each other's costs.
mission.objective: Write report.txt, exactly in this layout, every line 33 characters wide with no tabs and no trailing spaces: line 1 TEAM left-aligned in 20 columns, a space, COST (USD) right-aligned in 12 columns; line 2 a rule of 20 dashes, a space and 12 dashes; then one line per team of costs.csv in file order: the team name without surrounding spaces, left-aligned in 20 columns (a name longer than 20 characters is cut to its first 19 followed by ~), a space, the cost right-aligned in 12 columns with exactly 2 decimals; then the rule again; and last TOTAL in the same layout with the sum of all costs.

mission.name: Ledger Rollup
mission.description: Accounting closes October and wants the ledger as a rollup report: the rows grouped by department and team, with a subtotal after every team, another after every department and a grand total at the end. ledger.csv comes from the accounting tool, which writes amounts like "1,234.50" (in quotes because of the comma) and refunds in parentheses: (45.00).
mission.objective: Write report.tsv, every line with 5 tab-separated columns and no header. The ledger rows: department, team, date, description, amount, grouped by department (A-Z), then team (A-Z), and within a team in the order of ledger.csv. Amounts everywhere as plain numbers with two decimals, refunds negative (1234.50, -45.00). After the last row of each team: department, team, TEAM TOTAL, an empty column, the team's sum. After the last team of each department: department, an empty column, DEPARTMENT TOTAL, an empty column, the department's sum. Last line: two empty columns, GRAND TOTAL, an empty column, the sum of everything. Leave ledger.csv unchanged.
concepts: END block for the last group

mission.name: Traffic Anomalies
mission.description: Monitoring exported 30 days of daily request counts per host to requests.csv (date,host,requests). The on-call team wants an anomaly check they can rerun on every month's export: web-01 serves a hundred times more requests than mail-01, so one fixed threshold is useless. The export has gaps (NaN or empty values).
mission.objective: Write an executable detect.sh that is run as ./detect.sh FILE and prints CSV to stdout: the header host,date,value,zscore, then one line per anomaly, sorted by host and then date. A value is an anomaly when it is more than 3 standard deviations above or below the mean of its own host, using the population standard deviation (divide by n) over that host's numeric values only. Values that are not numbers are left out of everything; a host whose values never change has no anomalies. value is copied as written, zscore = (value - mean) / sd with 2 decimals. Save its output for requests.csv as anomalies.csv. detect.sh will also be run on another file.

mission.name: Two Exports
mission.description: The invoice data in clean.tsv is final. Finance opens it in Excel, which needs a proper CSV and shows names like Zoë as ZoÃ« unless the file declares itself UTF-8. The API team wants the same records as JSON with real numbers. Some company names and notes contain commas and double quotes, and the ZIP codes of Massachusetts start with 0.
mission.objective: Write export.csv: the UTF-8 byte-order mark (bytes ef bb bf), then the header and every row of clean.tsv as RFC 4180 CSV: fields separated by commas, a field that contains a comma or a double quote enclosed in double quotes, and each double quote inside it doubled. Write export.json: one JSON array with one object per row of clean.tsv, in order, whose keys are the column names; id and amount are JSON numbers, every other value (zip included) is a string exactly as in clean.tsv. No byte-order mark in the JSON. Leave clean.tsv unchanged.

mission.name: ETL Audit
mission.description: Last night's ETL job loaded the invoices from source.csv into the warehouse; loaded.tsv is what actually arrived. Finance says the warehouse total doesn't match the billing system, yet the job log claims success because both files have the same number of rows. The loader writes ids in uppercase, separates fields with tabs and stores amounts in cents.
mission.objective: Write audit.txt with four sections, in this order, each starting with its header line: [missing] lists every invoice id in source.csv that is not in loaded.tsv; [duplicated] lists every id that occurs more than once in loaded.tsv (each id once); [changed] has one line 'id source_amount loaded_amount' for every invoice whose loaded amount differs from source.csv; [totals] has the two lines 'source <sum of source.csv>' and 'loaded <sum of all rows of loaded.tsv>'. Ids are written in lowercase as in source.csv, one per line and sorted within each section; all amounts in units with exactly two decimals (1520.00). Leave both input files unchanged.

mission.name: What Does GRUB Boot?
mission.description: After last night's update the server came back up on an older kernel, and the team wants to know what GRUB boots by default. The rescue system has the server's disk copied into sysroot/.
mission.objective: From sysroot/boot/grub/grub.cfg, find the menu entry GRUB boots by default. Write its exact title (the text between the quotes after menuentry) to default_entry.txt and the kernel version it loads (as in the vmlinuz file name) to default_kernel.txt. Leave grub.cfg alone.

mission.name: Which Initramfs Lacks NVMe?
mission.description: Since the system disk moved to an NVMe drive, one of the installed kernels drops to the (initramfs) prompt at boot. The three initrd images of the old server are in sysroot/boot/.
mission.objective: Find which of the sysroot/boot/initrd.img-* images does not contain the nvme driver module (nvme.ko, not just nvme-core.ko) and write its file name, for example initrd.img-6.8.0-45-generic, to bad_initrd.txt. Do not modify the images.

mission.name: Sudo Cannot Resolve Host
mission.description: You booted a rescue system and the broken server's disk is mounted at sysroot/. The admins renamed the server last week, and now sudo on it complains "unable to resolve host". The rescue system has its own etc/ too, so mind which one you edit.
mission.objective: Fix the server's sysroot/etc/hosts so the 127.0.1.1 line carries the name found in the server's sysroot/etc/hostname. Keep every other line of that file. The rescue system's own etc/hosts and etc/hostname must stay unchanged. The helper ./sudo-in-sysroot true shows what sudo on the server would say.

mission.name: Boot Without a GUI
mission.description: The server is headless but its default boot target is graphical.target, so it waits for a display manager that is not installed. The server's disk is mounted at sysroot/ in the rescue system.
mission.objective: Make the server boot to multi-user.target by default: sysroot/etc/systemd/system/default.target must be a symlink that, read on the booted machine, points at the multi-user.target unit file under /usr/lib/systemd/system. Do not change the unit files.

mission.name: Offline Filesystem Repair
mission.description: After a power cut the data volume image data.img (an ext4 filesystem labelled datavol, not mounted anywhere) reports errors. The change ticket needs the repair output and the exit code as evidence.
mission.objective: Repair data.img offline so that a read-only check of it reports a clean filesystem. Keep the full output of the repair run in fsck.log, and write the exit code of that same repair run (just the number) to fsck_exit.txt. The filesystem UUID must stay the same.

mission.name: What Failed on Boot?
mission.description: Red [FAILED] lines scrolled past on the console during the last boot of the server, and nobody wrote them down. The console output was saved in sysroot/var/log/boot.log, escape codes and all.
mission.objective: Write failed_units.txt: the unit name of every unit that has a [FAILED] line in sysroot/var/log/boot.log (the name systemctl status takes, such as foo.service), one per line, in the order they first failed, each unit once. Units that only got a Dependency failed line did not fail themselves.

mission.name: Kernel Cleanup in /boot
mission.description: /boot is 98 % full and the next kernel update fails. Six kernels are installed on the server (its disk is mounted at sysroot/). Keep the one the server is running right now (uname-r.txt) and the newest installed one, and remove the rest.
mission.objective: In sysroot/, remove every kernel except the running one and the newest installed one: their vmlinuz-, initrd.img-, config-, System.map- files in boot/ and the lib/modules/<version>/ directories. Then make the links in boot/ right: vmlinuz and initrd.img point at the newest kernel, vmlinuz.old and initrd.img.old at the running one. Leave everything else in boot/ alone.

mission.name: Who Still Needs a Reboot?
mission.description: Patch night is over, and some servers installed a new kernel without rebooting into it. fleet/<host>/ holds each server's uname -a output and the dpkg listing of its linux-image packages.
mission.objective: Write reboot_needed.txt: the hostnames (one per line, sorted) of the servers whose running kernel is older than the newest kernel they have installed. Use the kernel release uname reports as the running one, and count only packages that are really installed (state ii) and are kernel images, not meta-packages or headers.

mission.name: Which Modules Went Missing?
mission.description: The RAID array did not assemble after a reboot. You have lsmod captures from a healthy twin server (healthy.lsmod) and from the broken host (broken.lsmod).
mission.objective: Write missing.txt: the names of the modules loaded on the healthy twin but not on the broken host (one per line, any order). Write load_first.txt: the one name among them whose loading would pull in all the others as dependencies.

mission.name: The Driver That Never Loads
mission.description: The new 10 GbE NIC driver ixgbe will not load on the server, not even by hand. The server's disk is mounted at sysroot/, and the helper ./modprobe-sim reads its module database and modprobe.d configuration the way the real modprobe would (it never loads anything).
mission.objective: Find what in sysroot/etc/modprobe.d/ stops ixgbe from loading and neutralise only that (comment it out or remove it), so that ./modprobe-sim -n -v ixgbe prints its insmod chain. Change nothing else in modprobe.d, and leave the helper alone.

mission.name: Which Disk Is Failing?
mission.description: The server boots slowly and /srv is read-only afterwards. Someone saved the kernel ring buffer as dmesg.txt before powering it off. It has three SATA disks and an optical drive, and the kernel names the same disk differently in different places.
mission.objective: Find the disk that is failing and write one line, "DEVICE SECONDS", to failing_disk.txt: the sdX name of the disk and the timestamp (as printed in the brackets, without the brackets) of the earliest error message the kernel logged about it, for example "sdz 12.345678". Do not modify dmesg.txt.

mission.name: Firmware Boots the Network
mission.description: After a firmware update the server tries a network (PXE) boot instead of Ubuntu. The rescue system cannot touch the real NVRAM, so ./efibootmgr here is a mock holding a captured copy of the boot entries, and blkid.txt is the captured partition list of the server's current disks.
mission.objective: Put the working Ubuntu entry first in the BootOrder stored by ./efibootmgr and keep all the other entries in their current relative order. The working entry is the one whose disk partition (PARTUUID) exists in blkid.txt. Do not delete or edit the entries themselves.

mission.name: Which Boot Died?
mission.description: The previous on-call merged two journal exports into journal.json (one JSON object per line, several boots, so the file is not in time order). One of those boots ended without shutting down cleanly: nobody remembers which, and the post-mortem needs its errors.
mission.objective: Write the _BOOT_ID of the boot that has no final systemd-shutdown message ("Powering off." or "Rebooting.") to crashed_boot.txt. Write that boot's messages of priority error or worse (journal PRIORITY 0 to 3), the MESSAGE text only, one per line in time order, to crash_errors.txt.

mission.name: Every Boot Ends in Emergency Mode
mission.description: The disks are fine, yet every boot of this server ends in emergency mode. A colleague was debugging a boot hang last week and left an option behind. The server's disk is mounted at sysroot/; update-grub in this folder is a mock that regenerates sysroot/boot/grub/grub.cfg from the settings the way the real tool does.
mission.objective: Remove the debug option that forces emergency mode from the GRUB settings in sysroot/etc/default, wherever it is set, and regenerate sysroot/boot/grub/grub.cfg with ./update-grub. No linux line may contain it any more, and every other kernel argument must still be there. Editing grub.cfg directly does not count.

mission.name: Timed Out Waiting for Device
mission.description: The server was cloned onto new disks and now stops in emergency mode with "Timed out waiting for device". The clone changed every filesystem UUID, but /etc/fstab still holds the old ones. The disk is mounted at sysroot/; blkid.txt and lsblk.txt are captures of the new disks, and ./fstab-lint checks sysroot/etc/fstab against them.
mission.objective: Fix sysroot/etc/fstab so every entry is valid: each source must name the volume that belongs to that mount point (the comment above each entry says what it was: match by label and size), the type must match what blkid.txt reports, every option must exist, and every mount point must exist in sysroot/. The removable backup disk at /mnt/backup must never be able to block boot again. Keep all five entries; ./fstab-lint must report no problems.

mission.name: Boots Without Network
mission.description: After a mainboard swap the server boots without network. The new board has new MAC addresses and the kernel names its NICs differently. The server's systemd-networkd files are in sysroot/etc/systemd/network/, the captured output of ip -o link from the rescue system is in ip-o-link.txt and the address plan is in ticket.txt.
mission.objective: Fix the .network files in sysroot/etc/systemd/network/ so each of the two new NICs is matched by exactly one file and gets the address and prefix from the ticket. The LAN interface must have the ticket's gateway, and that gateway must lie inside its subnet. The backup interface gets no gateway. Keep the DNS setting, and leave no file that still matches an old NIC name or the old board's MAC address.

mission.name: Why Does Boot Take 2.5 Minutes?
mission.description: A server takes two and a half minutes to boot. The previous admin saved the output of systemd-analyze blame (blame.txt), systemd-analyze critical-chain (critical-chain.txt) and the summary line (startup.txt). The server's disk is mounted at sysroot/.
mission.objective: Write the name of the unit that really delays the boot (not just one that takes long) to slow_unit.txt. Then fix it without editing the vendor unit under sysroot/usr/lib: add a drop-in in sysroot/etc/systemd/system/ so that the unit's ExecStart is replaced by a command that no longer waits up to two minutes.

mission.name: Roll Back /etc/app
mission.description: An upgrade broke the configuration in /etc/app, and the newest nightly snapshot was taken after the upgrade. snapshots/daily.N/ hold the server's earlier copies of etc/app (daily.0 is the newest), the live tree is sysroot/etc/app, and ./app --check-config [DIR] tells whether a configuration directory is valid.
mission.objective: Find the newest snapshot whose etc/app passes ./app --check-config and restore sysroot/etc/app from it: same files and nothing else (files added after the upgrade must be gone), with modes, symlink targets and modification times preserved. Nothing outside sysroot/etc/app may change, and the snapshots stay as they are.

mission.name: The EFI Partition Is Gone
mission.description: A bad partitioning script wiped the EFI system partition: sysroot/boot/efi is empty and the server cannot boot. Nightly tarballs of /boot are in backups/ (newest name last), and EFI.SHA256SUMS lists the checksums of the files that belong in EFI/. Some backups may be damaged.
mission.objective: Restore sysroot/boot/efi/EFI/ from the newest backup that is intact, so that every file passes EFI.SHA256SUMS (checked from sysroot/boot/efi) and keeps its mode. Extract only the EFI/ tree: the rest of sysroot/boot is newer than the backups and must not change, and no extra or doubly nested paths may appear.

mission.name: Links That Only Work on the Rescue Host
mission.description: The rescue copy of the server's root filesystem in sysroot/ came from rsync, with all its symlinks. The links are meant for the server: an absolute target like /usr/bin/x means the server's /usr/bin/x, not the rescue system's. Several links are broken on the server, and some that look broken from here work there.
mission.objective: Write to broken_links.txt, sorted, one per line, the path (relative to sysroot/, for example usr/bin/foo) of every symlink in sysroot/ that is broken as the server will see it, as found (before your repairs). Loops count as broken. Then repair the three links in sysroot/etc/alternatives that point at versions that no longer exist, so they resolve to the versions that are installed. Change nothing else.

mission.name: The Rescue Toolkit Will Not Start
mission.description: The rescue toolkit in rescue/ carries its own jq, loader (rescue/ld.so) and libraries (rescue/usr/lib/<arch dir>). In this rescue system jq fails with "error while loading shared libraries" when it runs with the toolkit's libraries, and a library is missing from the toolkit. The package cache pkgcache/ holds .deb files of the library packages.
mission.objective: Find the library that rescue/usr/bin/jq needs and the toolkit lacks, and restore it into the rescue library directory from the right package in pkgcache/, including its SONAME link, so that every library jq needs is there. Afterwards rescue/ld.so --library-path <that directory> rescue/usr/bin/jq must work and load every library from it. Do not change the jq binary or the loader.

mission.name: Command Not Found for Everything
mission.description: After a colleague edited the login files, user deploy on the broken server gets "command not found" for nearly everything. The server's disk is mounted at sysroot/; ./login-sim USER shows the PATH a login of that user gets, built from the captured login files the way the server reads them.
mission.objective: Fix the files under sysroot/etc (environment, profile.d) and the dotfiles in sysroot/home/deploy until ./login-sim deploy and ./login-sim ops both print the agreed PATH: /usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin followed by the application's /opt/<app>/bin directory (its name is in the profile files). No empty components, no duplicates, and the application directory only after the system directories.

mission.name: Nobody Can SSH In as ops
mission.description: Nobody can SSH in as ops on the broken server, and the rescue boot's auth.log shows several different refusals. The server's disk is mounted at sysroot/ (its log is sysroot/var/log/auth.log). bin/usermod and bin/chage here are mocks that edit the accounts in sysroot/ instead of this system.
mission.objective: Find every cause in sysroot/ and fix them all, so that ops can log in with the key in its authorized_keys: its shell must exist and be listed in /etc/shells, /etc/nologin must be gone, its account must no longer be expired, and the key must pass sshd's StrictModes check (home directory 755, .ssh 700, authorized_keys 600). Change nothing else: no other user's passwd or shadow line, and not ops' password hash.

mission.name: Pre-Reboot Checklist
mission.description: Before tonight's reboot window the team wants a script that tells, from a mounted root filesystem and without rebooting, whether the machine will come back. roots/healthy and roots/broken are two captured roots to test with: each has boot/grub/grub.cfg, boot/, etc/fstab, blkid.txt (captured blkid), df.txt (captured df -BM /boot) and etc/systemd/system/default.target.
mission.objective: Write prereboot.sh ROOT. It prints exactly four lines, in this order: PASS or FAIL followed by grub-default, fstab-uuids, default-target and boot-free. grub-default passes when the kernel and the initrd of GRUB's default entry exist under ROOT (the default is the set default= value: a number counting top-level entries from 0, where the submenu counts as one, or a path like 1>2 into a submenu). fstab-uuids passes when every UUID=, LABEL= and /dev/ source in ROOT/etc/fstab is found in ROOT/blkid.txt (UUIDs compare regardless of letter case; other sources are ignored). default-target passes when ROOT/etc/systemd/system/default.target resolves to a file inside ROOT (absolute link targets are relative to ROOT). boot-free passes when /boot has at least 100 MB available in ROOT/df.txt. The exit status is the number of FAIL lines. It is tested on five hidden roots.

mission.name: Vendor Asks: What Kernel?
mission.description: A hardware vendor's support desk will not open a case until you tell them exactly what this box runs. The ticket (TICKET.md) asks for three facts, and a half-filled template, facts.env, is already in the sandbox.
mission.objective: Fill in facts.env so that KERNEL_NAME is the kernel name, KERNEL_RELEASE is the kernel release and ARCH is the machine hardware name of this machine, exactly as the system reports them. Keep one KEY=value per line; comment lines may stay.

mission.name: Who Am I?
mission.description: This box's logs arrive in central logging under the name CHANGEME, so nobody can tell which machine they belong to. The log agent's config (agent.conf) still has the placeholder.
mission.objective: Set the active `hostname =` line in agent.conf to the hostname this machine's kernel reports right now. Every other line, including the commented examples, must stay exactly as it is.

mission.name: Who Was On the Jump Host?
mission.description: Security snapshotted the jump host during an incident and kept its login records as capture/utmp (the binary file behind `who`). They want to know who was connected from outside the corporate 10.0.0.0/8 network.
mission.objective: From capture/utmp, write outside_sessions.txt with one line per remote session whose source address is NOT inside 10.0.0.0/8, formatted `user tty host`, in the order `who` lists them. Local console sessions (no host) are not remote and are not listed. Plain `who` shows this machine, not the capture.

mission.name: Warn the Active Users
mission.description: The shared build box is about to be rebooted. Before you do it, you want to warn whoever is actually working on it, not the people who left a terminal open last week. A colleague pasted the output of `w` into capture/w.txt.
mission.objective: From capture/w.txt, write warn_users.txt: the users with at least one session idle for LESS than 10 minutes, one name per line, sorted, each name once. Sessions idle for exactly 10 minutes or more do not count.

mission.name: Why Did It Reboot?
mission.description: db-02 rebooted on its own several times this autumn and management wants numbers. Its login history (the binary /var/log/wtmp) was copied to capture/wtmp. The live `last` on this machine reads an empty log and tells you nothing.
mission.objective: From capture/wtmp, write two files. reboots.txt: just the number of reboots recorded in October 2026. crash_users.txt: the users (sorted, each once) whose sessions were cut off by a crash during an October reboot, one name per line. Sessions that ended cleanly, or at a clean shutdown ("down"), do not count, and neither do September or November events.
concepts: crash vs down vs still logged in

mission.name: What Was It Started With?
mission.description: The running `worker` process behaves like a staging worker (wrong database, test data), although its config file says production. Somebody started it by hand with environment variables that override the file. You need the values it is really using (TICKET.md).
mission.objective: Find the running worker process and write the APP_ENV and DB_HOST it was actually started with to worker_env.txt, as two lines `APP_ENV=...` and `DB_HOST=...` (in that order). Use the process's environment, not the config file and not your own shell. A second, unrelated process (worker-metrics) is running too.

mission.name: End-of-Life Audit
mission.description: Compliance wants to know which of the 15 servers still run an operating system that is past its end-of-life date as of 2026-11-10. Each server's /etc was captured under fleet/<host>/etc/, and eol.csv lists the end-of-life date of each distribution release.
mission.objective: Write eol_hosts.txt with one line `host ID VERSION_ID` for every host whose OS reached end of life on or before 2026-11-10, sorted by host name. ID and VERSION_ID are the values from the host's os-release, without quotes. eol.csv is keyed by distribution ID and major version.
concepts: sourcing a file in a subshell

mission.name: Licence by Core
mission.description: The database vendor licenses per physical core, and procurement has to report the capacity of three servers before the audit. Nobody can log in to them, but their /proc/cpuinfo was saved under capture/ (see TICKET.md).
mission.objective: Write licence.csv with the header `host,sockets,cores,threads` and one row per host (in the order of the files, sorted by host name): sockets = distinct physical CPUs as the file reports them, cores = distinct physical cores in total (hyperthreads of one core count once), threads = logical CPUs.

mission.name: Where Did the Memory Go?
mission.description: Four app servers raised a 'low memory' alert, but the on-call engineer thinks some of them are fine. Their /proc/meminfo files were saved under capture/ before anyone restarted anything.
mission.objective: Write memory.csv with the header `host,available_mib,consumer` and one row per host (sorted by host). available_mib is MemAvailable in whole MiB (rounded down). consumer is the largest of three non-application consumers, written as HugePages (HugePages_Total x Hugepagesize), Shmem or SUnreclaim.

mission.name: Permission Denied on a Mount
mission.description: CI builds on ci-runner-3 fail with "Permission denied" when they run ./configure in /var/lib/ci/work/build-42, although the file is executable and owned by the CI user. Someone suspects the mount options. The mount table was saved as capture/mountinfo (the content of /proc/self/mountinfo).
mission.objective: Find which mount the path /var/lib/ci/work/build-42 really lives on and write one line `target source fstype options` to mount.txt. Take the mount that is in effect (a later mount at the same place hides an earlier one). Write source the way findmnt shows it, including the bind-mounted subdirectory in square brackets when there is one, and options as the mount's own options (noexec must show up).
concepts: bind mounts and the root field

mission.name: Pull the Right Disk
mission.description: Monitoring says the disk with the serial number in TICKET.md is failing and the datacentre technician is waiting to pull it. Two disks in the box are the same model, so the model name will not tell them apart. The output of `lsblk -J` was saved to capture/lsblk.json (TICKET.md names the serial).
mission.objective: Write disk.txt: the first line is the device path of the failing whole disk (/dev/NAME, from the serial in TICKET.md), followed by every real mount path that still lives on that disk (partitions, and logical volumes or other devices stacked on them), one per line, sorted. Swap and unmounted devices are not paths and are left out; a device with several mount points contributes all of them.

mission.name: No Driver, No Link
mission.description: The new 25 GbE card in storage-07 does not show up as a network interface after the hardware swap. A technician saved the output of `lspci -nnk` to capture/lspci.txt. Before anyone orders a new card, you want to know which network and storage devices have no driver bound at all, and which kernel module could drive them.
mission.objective: Write unbound.txt with one line per device that is a network controller (PCI class 02xx) or a storage controller (class 01xx) and has no `Kernel driver in use:`, formatted `slot [vendor:device] module`, in the order of the file. module is the first one listed on the device's `Kernel modules:` line, or a single - when the device lists none. Bridges, USB controllers, graphics and everything else are out of scope.
concepts: Kernel driver in use vs Kernel modules

mission.name: Unlisted USB Storage
mission.description: Policy on the workstation fleet allows only listed USB mass-storage devices. Security saved the USB part of /sys from ws-114 as capture/sys, and the approved devices are in usb-allowlist.txt (see TICKET.md).
mission.objective: Find every USB mass-storage device in capture/sys that is not on the allowlist and write rogue_usb.txt with one line per device, formatted `port vid:pid product` (for example `1-4 0781:5581 Ultra`), using the lowercase ids and the product string from sysfs. A device with several storage interfaces is one line. Hubs, interfaces and devices that merely look similar to an allowlisted one are not to be mixed up.

mission.name: Kill the Whole Tree
mission.description: A self-healing job runner has a worker stuck on job 7. Every layer of the runner restarts what dies below it, so killing the worker alone changes nothing (see TICKET.md).
mission.objective: Write the chain of PIDs from the worker running `--job 7` up to the top-level supervisor.sh into chain.txt, one PID per line, the worker first and supervisor.sh last. Then stop the entire job runner (supervisor, dispatcher, shards and every worker) so that nothing is running or respawning two seconds later. Record the chain before you kill anything.

mission.name: The Listener Nobody Approved
mission.description: The nightly port scan found one more TCP listener on app-03 than the inventory knows. approved.txt lists the approved services; the extra one may be hiding behind a familiar name (see TICKET.md).
mission.objective: Find the one listening TCP socket on this machine whose port is not in approved.txt, write `port pid exe` to rogue.txt (exe is the real executable path of that process), and stop that process. All approved services, including the one that listens on IPv6 only, must keep running.

mission.name: Port to Unit Inventory
mission.description: For the security review you need to know which systemd unit is behind every listening TCP port of web-03. A teammate captured `ss -ltnpH`, every PID's cgroup file and the unit files from the production host (see TICKET.md).
mission.objective: Write inventory.csv from the captures in capture/: the header line `port,proto,unit`, then one row per listening port (proto is always `tcp`; IPv4 and IPv6 listeners of one port are a single row), sorted numerically by port. The unit is the last component of the cgroup path of the process that owns the socket (for example `nginx.service` or `session-7.scope`); where only systemd (PID 1) holds the socket, it is the service that the matching .socket unit activates.

mission.name: Tune for the Search Vendor
mission.description: The search engine vendor lists kernel settings its cluster nodes must have. This node already meets some of them, and config management owns the rest of the system (see TICKET.md and vendor-requirements.txt).
mission.objective: Write sysctl.d/90-search.conf (`key = value` lines) containing only the settings from vendor-requirements.txt that this machine does NOT meet right now, each with a value that meets the requirement. A setting that already complies must not appear, and no value may be lowered. The file is only prepared; do not try to apply it.

mission.name: Which File Wins?
mission.description: k8s-node-12 behaves as if net.ipv4.ip_forward were 0, although /etc/sysctl.conf sets it to 1. The node's sysctl configuration was captured under capture/ (see TICKET.md).
mission.objective: Work out, for every key set anywhere in capture/ (etc/sysctl.conf, etc/sysctl.d, run/sysctl.d, usr/lib/sysctl.d), the value systemd-sysctl ends up applying and the file that set it. Write effective.txt with one line `key=value path` per key, sorted by key. Write keys with dots, collapse repeated spaces inside values, and give the path under capture/ as systemd finds the file (on this Ubuntu node etc/sysctl.d/99-sysctl.conf is a symlink to ../sysctl.conf, and it counts under that name). Keys that only a hidden file sets are not applied and must not be listed.

mission.name: Too Many Open Files
mission.description: The `indexer` process crashes under load with "Too many open files". It runs as a systemd service, and sysroot/ is a copy of the host's /etc (see TICKET.md). The running process is the evidence.
mission.objective: Write limits.txt with three lines, `soft=`, `hard=` (the soft and hard "open files" limits of the running indexer) and `open=` (how many file descriptors it has open right now). Then make the fix that works for a systemd service inside sysroot/: a drop-in for indexer.service that gives it LimitNOFILE=65536 effectively. Do not restart or kill the indexer.
concepts: limits.conf only applies to PAM sessions

mission.name: Who Hit the Wall?
mission.description: Two containers were OOM-killed overnight on node-21 and a third service is crawling. Capacity planning wants the cgroup numbers from the captured cgroup v2 tree under cgroup/system.slice/ (see TICKET.md).
mission.objective: Write cgroups.csv with the header `unit,memory_max_mib,oom_kills,throttled_pct` and one row per unit directory of cgroup/system.slice/ (sorted by unit). memory_max_mib is the memory limit in MiB, or the word `unlimited` when there is none; oom_kills is the number of processes the OOM killer killed in that cgroup; throttled_pct is the share of CPU periods in which the cgroup was throttled, in percent with one decimal (0.0 when there were no periods).

mission.name: Own PID, Host Network
mission.description: A container that has its own PID namespace but shares the host's network namespace can reach every host service on localhost. Security captured `lsns -J` and `ps -eo pid,user,pidns,netns,comm` from docker-host-04 (see TICKET.md).
mission.objective: From capture/lsns.json and capture/ps.txt, write host_net.txt with one line `pid comm` (ascending by PID) for every process that is in its own PID namespace (not the host's) while running in the host's network namespace. The host's namespaces are the ones PID 1 lives in.

mission.name: The Space That du Cannot See
mission.description: The tmp/ usage alarm says it grew by about 50 MB, but `du` finds only a few MB. A process still holds a deleted debug log open (see TICKET.md).
mission.objective: Recover the lost debug log into recovered/app-debug.log (byte for byte), stop the process that holds it, and clean tmp/ by policy: delete regular files older than 7 days that no process has open. Newer files, and files or sockets a live process is using, must stay.

mission.name: What Is It Really?
mission.description: The incident team copied 40 files from a compromised host into quarantine/. The attacker chose the names, so the extensions lie (see TICKET.md).
mission.objective: Write types.tsv with one line `name<TAB>class` per file in quarantine/ (name without the directory), where class is one of: `elf` (compiled executable), `script` (text starting with a #! line), `image` (PNG, JPEG or GIF), `text` (any other plain text, even if its name says .sh or .exe), or `archive:<class>` for a gzip/bzip2/xz compressed file, naming the class of what it contains.

mission.name: One Script to Inspect Them All
mission.description: The fleet inventory needs one portable script that describes any Linux host it runs on as a JSON document. You will write it as a normal user (see TICKET.md for the exact report format).
mission.objective: Write inspect.sh so that running it prints one JSON object with the keys hostname, kernel, arch, os_id, os_version, cpus, mem_total_mib, root_use_pct, uptime_seconds and listening_ports, as described in TICKET.md. Values come from the machine each time it runs; numbers are JSON numbers, os_version is a string, and listening_ports lists this user's TCP listener ports ascending (an empty array when there are none).

mission.name: Append, Don't Overwrite
mission.description: The nightly maintenance script prints a report, and compliance wants it kept in audit.log, which already holds six months of history. Last quarter someone ran the script into the log with a plain redirect and the old entries were gone for good.
mission.objective: Run ./maintenance.sh once so that its complete output (what it prints normally and what it prints as warnings) both appears on your screen and is added to the end of audit.log. The existing history in audit.log must stay exactly as it is, and maintenance.sh must not be edited.

mission.name: Thumbnails With Awkward Names
mission.description: The photo server is running out of space, and the cached thumbnails under photos/ are safe to delete. A teammate already tried a quick find-and-xargs one-liner and it died halfway with an error about quotes.
mission.objective: Delete every regular file whose name ends in .thumb anywhere under photos/ (including the ones with spaces, quotes or even a newline in the name). Every other file, and every directory, must stay exactly as it is.
concepts: file names with spaces and quotes

mission.name: Fixed-Width Billing Import
mission.description: The legacy billing importer reads positions, not delimiters, and rejects a file if even one line is a character off. Finance exported accounts.csv and needs it converted.
mission.objective: Write billing.dat from accounts.csv (skip the header line): one line per account, in the same order, formatted as ACCT, the account id as 6 digits with leading zeros, a |, the name left-aligned in exactly 12 characters (longer names are cut to 12), a |, and the amount right-aligned in 10 characters with two decimals. Example: ACCT000042|Acme Corp   |    149.50

mission.name: Labels for the B-Side PDUs
mission.description: The datacenter team is printing labels for the second power feed. Each PDU outlet gets a label naming its rack position, and the label printer sorts them as text, so the numbers must all have two digits.
mission.objective: Read the rack and range in label-request.txt and write labels.txt with one label per line, in the form rack-<letter>-<NN>, for every second position (the start, then every 2nd after it) up to the last one, numbers always two digits, e.g. rack-a-02. No other lines.

mission.name: Unattended Installer, Thousand Pings
mission.description: The vendor installer ./install.sh asks for confirmation again and again, and the deployment pipeline has nobody to type the answers. QA also wants a load-test fixture with a thousand identical lines.
mission.objective: Run ./install.sh so it completes without you answering any question by hand (it writes install.done when it succeeds), and create load.txt containing exactly 1000 lines, each one the word ping.

mission.name: Line Numbers Like the Editor
mission.description: A reviewer left comments on nginx.conf that cite line numbers from their editor ('line 57: why is this open to the world?'). The file you were given has no numbers, and anyone reading the review needs the same numbering.
mission.objective: Write review.txt: every line of nginx.conf, blank lines included, numbered as an editor would (the first line is 1, and blank lines count). Format each line as the number right-aligned in 3 characters, a colon, a space, then the original line, e.g. '  7: server {'. Keep nginx.conf unchanged.
concepts: nl skips blank lines by default

mission.name: Newest Release First
mission.description: The changelog CHANGES was appended to for years, oldest release at the top. The website wants it newest first. Each release is a block of several lines introduced by a ---- line, and the lines inside a block are in a deliberate order.
mission.objective: Write CHANGES.newest-first: the same release blocks as CHANGES in reverse order (the last block first), with every block's own lines in their original order, and each block still introduced by its ---- line, exactly as in the original. Keep CHANGES unchanged.

mission.name: Traffic Per Registrable Domain
mission.description: Marketing wants to know which sites send the most traffic, per registrable domain: shop.example.com and www.example.com count as example.com, but shop.bbc.co.uk counts as bbc.co.uk. The 5,000 request URLs in urls.txt come with ports, paths, queries, odd capitalization and the occasional trailing dot.
mission.objective: Write domains.txt with one line per registrable domain, as: the request count, a single space, the domain in lowercase. The registrable domain is the last two labels of the host, or the last three when the last two are listed in two-level-suffixes.txt (co.uk and the like). Sort by count, highest first; domains with the same count in plain byte order (LC_ALL=C sort). No other lines; leading spaces are ignored.

mission.name: Seventy Characters per SMS
mission.description: The paging gateway accepts messages of at most 70 characters per line and rejects the whole alert if one line is longer. alert.txt has three long lines, one of which contains a link longer than 70 characters on its own.
mission.objective: Write alert.sms from alert.txt so that no line is longer than 70 characters, words are broken only where there is no other choice (a word longer than the limit has to be cut), and no text is lost or changed: apart from the inserted line breaks, alert.sms is identical to alert.txt, and the three original lines still end where they did.
concepts: hard break of an over-long word

mission.name: Reflow the Release Notes
mission.description: The release notes in NOTES.txt were drafted with one sentence per line, so the page looks ragged: some lines are tiny, others run past the margin. Paragraphs are separated by blank lines, and the bullet items (an indented list, items separated by blank lines) must stay separate bullets.
mission.objective: Write NOTES.wrapped: the text of NOTES.txt reflowed so no line is longer than 72 characters and lines are filled (consecutive short lines of a paragraph or bullet are joined). The words stay the same and in the same order, every paragraph and every bullet item stays a unit of its own, and each bullet still starts on its own line beginning with two spaces and '- '.
concepts: paragraphs are separated by blank lines

mission.name: YAML Forbids Tabs
mission.description: The CI linter rejects deploy.yaml: 'found character that cannot start any token'. An editor indented parts of the file with tabs, sometimes mixed with spaces. YAML allows only spaces for indentation, but two values in the file contain a real tab on purpose.
mission.objective: Fix deploy.yaml in place so that no line has a tab in its indentation: each indentation level must end up as 2 spaces, whatever mix of tabs and spaces it was written with (a tab advances to the next multiple of 2 columns). The tab characters inside the quoted values (banner and message) must stay, and nothing else in the file may change. The untouched original is kept as deploy.yaml.orig.

mission.name: Missing Separator
mission.description: Someone opened the Makefile in an editor that replaces tabs with spaces, and make now stops with 'Makefile:14: *** missing separator'. Recipe lines must start with a tab. But the file also has lines indented with 8 spaces that are not recipes: the continuation of a variable and some indented comments. They must stay as they are.
mission.objective: Fix Makefile in place: every recipe line (an 8-space-indented line that follows a 'target:' line, including its continuation lines) must start with one tab instead of the 8 spaces. Variable continuation lines and indented comments keep their 8 spaces, and nothing else changes. The untouched original is kept as Makefile.orig.

mission.name: A Sample You Can Redraw
mission.description: The auditor wants 25 random transactions from this quarter's export. Next month she will ask for 'the same 25 again' to compare against corrected data, so the draw has to be repeatable.
mission.objective: Write sample.csv with 25 transactions drawn at random from tx.csv, header line excluded (the header must not be in the sample and must not be a candidate). The draw must be reproducible: use seed.bin as the source of randomness, so anyone who repeats the draw with the same file and the same command gets the same 25 lines in the same order.

mission.name: Five Thousand At A Time
mission.description: The CRM import API rejects any CSV with more than 5,000 data rows, and it needs the header line in every file it receives. customers.csv has 23,417 customers.
mission.objective: Cut customers.csv into the directory chunks/ as part-00.csv, part-01.csv, part-02.csv and so on. Every chunk must start with the header line and hold at most 5,000 data rows, the chunks must be as full as possible (no more files than needed), and the data rows of all chunks put back together must equal the data rows of customers.csv.

mission.name: One File Per Resource
mission.description: A cluster export, all.yaml, holds 14 Kubernetes manifests in one stream separated by --- lines. The GitOps repository wants one file per resource, named after what it is.
mission.objective: Split all.yaml into the directory manifests/ so that each of the 14 resources has its own file named <kind>-<name>.yaml, with kind in lower case and name taken from the resource's own metadata (for a Deployment named web: deployment-web.yaml). Each file holds exactly the lines of its document, without the --- separator line. There must be 14 files, none empty, and no leftovers from the splitting.

mission.name: What Does The Agent Phone Home To
mission.description: A vendor monitoring agent opens a connection nobody approved. There is no source, only the binary agent.bin. Security needs two facts from it: the endpoint it reports to and the licence ID baked into it.
mission.objective: Find the real endpoint URL and the real licence ID in agent.bin and write them to findings.txt as exactly two lines: endpoint=<url> and license=<id>. The binary also carries a block marked TEST (between TEST-BEGIN and TEST-END) with fixture values that look real but are not; they must not be reported. The licence ID is stored in a different text encoding from the rest of the strings.

mission.name: Reading Sensor Records By Hand
mission.description: A boiler sensor logger writes fixed-size binary records to sensors.bin. There is no viewer for this format, but FORMAT.txt describes it, and the plant engineer wants every record where the sensor reported a fault.
mission.objective: Decode sensors.bin according to FORMAT.txt and write faults.txt: one line per record whose status is not zero, in file order, as three space-separated fields: timestamp (decimal), sensor id and value. Values may be written with any reasonable number of decimals, the result is compared numerically.

mission.name: Flip One Byte, Fix One Sum
mission.description: Before flashing the controller, the engineer needs debug mode on in its 128-byte configuration blob. The bootloader refuses any blob whose checksum is wrong. The original is saved as config.bin.orig.
mission.objective: Patch config.bin so that the byte at offset 0x2A is 01 (it is 00 now). The last byte of the file is a checksum: the sum of all the bytes before it, modulo 256. Update it for the patched content. Exactly those two bytes may differ from config.bin.orig, and the size must stay 128 bytes.

mission.name: Secrets Must Be Base64, Exactly
mission.description: The new service reads its credentials from a Kubernetes Secret. The values are in plain files in this folder, and Kubernetes only accepts them base64-encoded, each on a single YAML line.
mission.objective: Write secret.yaml: a Secret (apiVersion v1, kind Secret, metadata name app-secrets, type Opaque) whose data section holds exactly three keys: db-password (the first line of password.txt, without its line ending), tls.crt (the whole file tls.crt) and logo.png (the whole file logo.png). Each value must be one unbroken base64 string that decodes to exactly the bytes of its source.

mission.name: Read It, Never Run It
mission.description: During a review someone found an odd line in suspicious.cron: it echoes a long blob, decodes it with base64 -d and pipes the result into sh. Incident response needs to know what it does, without running it.
mission.objective: Decode the blob in suspicious.cron safely (never pipe it to a shell) and write ioc.txt with exactly two lines: c2=<host the payload contacts> and dropped=<path of the file it writes>. The payload is a harmless training stub, but treat it as hostile.

mission.name: Why Are The Reports Slow
mission.description: Three report generators in reports/ are all described as 'slow', but the fix depends on why: one waits for something, one burns CPU, one drowns in tiny system calls. Time each of them and say which is which.
mission.objective: Run each reports/gen-*.sh once and record its timings in timings.txt: three lines (same order as ls reports/) of 'real user sys' in seconds with three decimals, for example '2.004 0.001 0.002'. Then write class.txt with three lines '<script name> <class>' in the same order, where class is cpu (computing), wait (idle, waiting) or syscall (dominated by system calls). The reports' output itself is not needed.

mission.name: A Program That Needs A Terminal
mission.description: Vendor support asked for a transcript of ./vendor-diag, but the tool only prints its report when it believes a person is watching: redirect it to a file and it quits. It also draws a spinner and colours with control characters, which turn into junk in a plain text file.
mission.objective: Record a session of ./vendor-diag into diag.typescript, with the real report in it (the tool must have run on a terminal). Then give support a clean diag.txt: only the report lines exactly as a person saw them on screen, without colour codes, carriage returns, spinner frames, or the 'Script started/done' lines the recorder adds. Tip for this game's shell: script forwards the shell's own input to the program, so start it with </dev/null, or press Ctrl-C if it seems stuck.

mission.name: Answer The Wizard Without A Human
mission.description: The provisioning wizard ./provision-wizard asks six questions, but it asks them in a different order every time and writes its prompts without a trailing newline. Ops wants it driven by a script from a pipeline. The answers are in answers.conf. (expect is not installed here: bash can do the job.)
mission.objective: Write answer.sh in this folder. When run with 'bash answer.sh', it must start ./provision-wizard, read each question as it appears, give the matching value from answers.conf, and let the wizard finish so that provision.result is written with the six answers. The check runs answer.sh five times, with the questions in five different orders, and each run must finish within 10 seconds. Do not edit provision-wizard.

mission.name: Unpack The Support Bundle
mission.description: Support sent bundle.eml, one MIME message with an explanation and two attachments, and asked three questions that need the contents of all three parts. The labels in the headers cannot be fully trusted, and one attachment is in an encoding grep does not understand.
mission.objective: Write summary.txt with exactly three lines: 'errors: N' (the number of lines whose level is ERROR in the service log attachment), 'kernel: V' (the kernel version from the 'Linux version' line of the kernel log attachment) and 'setting: K=V' (the line marked 'Recommended setting' in the text part of the message; ignore the old value mentioned next to it). Decode every part yourself; work out what a part really is from its content, not from its Content-Type.

mission.name: Green Log, Empty Archive
mission.description: Nightly backups have reported success for a week, but the restore test found last night's archive nearly empty (see RESTORE-TEST.md).
mission.objective: Fix backup.sh so that, when cron runs it (a bare environment, started from some other directory), it archives the whole 'office share/data' tree into backups/ (hidden files and names with spaces included), and so that it exits non-zero when tar cannot read a file. Leave a fresh archive in backups/ that restores the tree exactly.

mission.name: Noisy Logs
mission.description: The application volume is at 95 % because app.log grows about a megabyte a minute. TICKET.md says the app must not be restarted.
mission.objective: Make the already running app (same process) log at warn again, free the space its log holds without deleting the file out from under it, and make rotate.conf valid (logrotate -d with logrotate.state reports no errors) for the log the app really writes, in a way that is safe for a process that keeps the file open.

mission.name: Friday's Change
mission.description: The service has not started since Friday's hand edit of config.json. TICKET.md describes the change that was approved, and config.json.last-good is the last version that worked.
mission.objective: Make ./app --check pass with a config.json that is the last-good config plus exactly the change in TICKET.md: nothing else may differ, not even a value the parser would silently accept.

mission.name: Twelve Parts and a Trojan
mission.description: The vendor's dataset arrived as a 12-part email attachment in incoming/, and one part was re-sent separately (VENDOR-NOTE.txt). Only the reports are needed for the audit.
mission.objective: Leave in restored/ exactly the dataset/reports/ subtree (paths kept under restored/dataset/reports/), with every file verified against the vendor's SHA256SUMS, and nothing else: no other part of the dataset, and nothing written outside restored/.

mission.name: Permission Chaos
mission.description: Someone ran chmod -R 777 on the app tree, then 'fixed' the secrets by hand; the app still cannot read its database password. POLICY.md and last month's getfacl dump (perms.acl) are the references.
mission.objective: Restore the tree under app/: every path that is in perms.acl must have exactly the mode and ACL it had there; every path created since then must follow POLICY.md; nothing may be left world-writable.

mission.name: Double Revenue
mission.description: The daily KPI mail has shown roughly double revenue and orders since Monday, when log rotation was changed (see TICKET.md).
mission.objective: Fix daily_report.sh so it gives finance's numbers: each successful checkout (POST /checkout answered 200) counted once, for today's logs (2026-11-10) and for any other day's logs placed next to the script. The report format must stay as it is.

mission.name: Secret Hunt
mission.description: A live payments key (pk_live_...) turned up on a public paste site. TICKET.md has the excerpt.
mission.objective: Create leaks.txt listing every location of that exact key under site/ (a path, or archive:member for tar members), and replace every copy in ordinary files with REDACTED (base64 copies and the key split by a line continuation included). Archives are listed but must stay byte-identical, as must everything that is not part of the leak. Keys that merely look alike are not ours.

mission.name: Cleanup Sprint
mission.description: var/ is full and the 09:00 batch needs the space. RETENTION.md says what may go, and the nightly batch job is running right now.
mission.objective: Apply RETENTION.md to var/: delete expired logs, gzip the logs the policy says to compress, delete expired core dumps, keep every .keep file, and leave everything the running batch job holds open exactly as it is (the job must stay running).

mission.name: Checksum Race
mission.description: The mirror sync ended 'with warnings'. README-MIRROR.md explains the layout; the upstream's SHA256SUMS came from another system, and one big file is still being uploaded.
mission.objective: Put only verified files into public/ (byte-identical, the in-flight file only once its upload is complete), and write rejected.txt with the name of every file listed in SHA256SUMS that is corrupt, truncated or missing, one per line. Do not publish partial files, and do not reject a file for being unfinished.

mission.name: Release Rollback
mission.description: The newest release (current) throws 500s and the previous one is no better. INCIDENT.md describes the layout; the app server is the mock ./appctl.
mission.objective: Roll back: current must be a link to the newest release that has no failed health checks, every release and its shared link must stay intact (nothing stray inside a release), and the app server must have been reloaded (./appctl reload) after the switch.

mission.name: Storage Panic
mission.description: Writes fail with 'No space left on device', but df -h shows plenty free (INCIDENT.md, df-h.txt and df-i.txt).
mission.objective: Clean the inode hog by the policy in INCIDENT.md (sessions older than one day are deleted, younger ones and everything else under var/ stay) and write the relative path of the directory that holds the most files into report.txt. vm.img must stay untouched.

mission.name: Cron Mess
mission.description: Half our cron jobs never run, one fires every minute between 2 and 3 am, and two backups overlapped last night. SCHEDULE.md says what each job should do.
mission.objective: Fix crontab.txt (and anything else the jobs need) so that ./cron-sim, which runs the table through a cron-like environment for one simulated day, reports every job exactly as SCHEDULE.md requires and exits 0.

mission.name: User Audit
mission.description: Three people left last month and OFFBOARD.md lists what must be cut off. The captured server state is in sysroot/, with the account tools in sysroot/bin.
mission.objective: In sysroot/: lock the three departed accounts in shadow, remove every copy of their keys from every authorized_keys (shared accounts included, whatever the comment says), remove the non-root account with UID 0, and write audit.txt with the findings in the form OFFBOARD.md defines. Nothing else about the system may change.

mission.name: Link Labyrinth
mission.description: The app reads a stale config, and since the release folders were renamed some paths fail ('No such file', 'Too many levels of symbolic links'). NOTES.md describes the intended layout of deploy/.
mission.objective: Make deploy/ match NOTES.md: no broken, looping or absolute links, editing releases/<new>/app.conf (in place or with an editor) changes what config/active.conf shows, the old release stays untouched, and the whole tree still works after being copied to another directory.

mission.name: Config Storm
mission.description: Config management pushed a broken template to all 12 services overnight (OVERNIGHT.md). The env files came from another system, and the live configs may contain changes someone made by hand.
mission.objective: Make every rendered/<service>.conf exactly template.conf with its ${NAME} placeholders filled from env/<service>.env (raw values, a bare $RUNTIME_DIR stays literal), and write drift.txt: the sorted list of services whose live/<service>.conf has real manual changes (comment and blank-line differences do not count). template.conf and live/ must stay untouched.

mission.name: Twelve Workers
mission.description: The spool volume on the ingest box is filling at several MB per second. Twelve processes are all called `worker`, they have the same command line, and the on-call before you already tried `pkill worker` once; the shift lead says that took the whole ingest pipeline down for ten minutes.
mission.objective: Stop the one runaway writer without touching any of the other eleven workers, delete the junk files it has been producing in spool/ (the legitimate spool/w*.log files must stay), and write culprit.txt with one line: the culprit's PID, a space, and the absolute path of its executable.

mission.name: Which deployctl?
mission.description: CI keeps deploying with deployctl 1.x even though 2.4.1 is installed, and on every laptop `deployctl --version` is fine. The pipeline's shell setup was written by three different people over two years.
mission.objective: Make the CI deploy (`./deploy-sim`, which runs the job exactly the way CI does) report `deployctl 2.4.1` and still print target=prod. Then write shadows.txt: the absolute path of every file that made CI pick the old version, one per line. Things that do not affect the CI run are not shadows. The old 1.x install must stay on disk (another team pins it), and deploy-sim itself must not be edited.

mission.name: Order 7f3a
mission.description: A customer says their order failed around 14:00 yesterday and support has only a truncated ID. TICKET.txt has the full order ID. The services log it in different spellings, some of the logs have rotated, and one of them makes grep complain.
mission.objective: Write trail.txt: every log line under logs/ (all five services, current files, rotations and compressed rotations) that mentions that order, copied verbatim, one per line, sorted by the time the event happened (oldest first). Lines about other orders, even ones that look similar, must not be in it. Do not modify anything under logs/.

mission.name: Invoice Mismatch
mission.description: Finance says the invoice totals do not match what the payment provider settled. Invoices are in several currencies (invoices.csv, amounts in units), the provider settles everything in EUR cents in a fixed-width file, and the daily rate table is in rates.csv. FORMAT.md describes the three files.
mission.objective: Write mismatch.csv: a header line `invoice,invoice_eur,provider_eur` followed by one line for every invoice whose amount converted to EUR (each invoice at the latest rate for its currency dated on or before the invoice date, rounded to cents) differs from the provider's settled amount by more than 0.01 EUR. Both amounts have two decimals, rows are sorted by invoice id.

mission.name: Audit Surgery
mission.description: Before the audit, all 40 service configs in conf/ must stop offering TLS 1.0 and 1.1 and must point at the new upstream port. The same keys also appear in other sections of these files, in commented-out examples, and not every file was written in the same style.
mission.objective: In every conf/*.conf: set `ssl_protocols` to `TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3` in the [tls] section only, and change the port from 8080 to 8443 in the [upstream] section only (an upstream port other than 8080 stays as it is). Everything else must stay byte-for-byte as it was: other sections, comments, spacing, line endings. Keep a `.bak` copy of the original next to each file you change (conf/svc-NN.conf.bak).

mission.name: Tar Tunnel
mission.description: alpha/data has to reach bravo, and the only channel between the two hosts is the text relay (./relay send): ASCII lines of at most 76 characters, messages of at most 64 KB. Whatever you send arrives in bravo/inbox/ as separate messages, in no particular order. The tree has binary files, symlinks, a hard-linked pair, odd modes and old modification times.
mission.objective: Get bravo/data into existence as an exact copy of alpha/data: same content, modes, symlinks, hard links (one inode, not two copies) and modification times. Use only the relay to move the data; alpha/data itself must stay unchanged.
concepts: split and reassembly with sequence numbers
hard links and symlinks in tar

mission.name: Back to Tuesday
mission.description: Ransomware hit the file share on Wednesday morning. The backup folder has Sunday's full archive and the incrementals GNU tar made each evening, plus the one taken after the alarm. One of the archives on the share is damaged; the offsite folder holds copies under different names. RUNBOOK.txt has the schedule.
mission.objective: Rebuild the share as it was on Tuesday at 18:00 in restored/ (create it): every file with its Tuesday content, nothing that was deleted before Tuesday evening, nothing from Wednesday. Do not modify anything in backups/ or offsite/.
concepts: restoring an incremental chain in order

mission.name: 502 After the Migration
mission.description: webapp was moved to the new host layout last night and now it will not stay up; customers get 502 from the proxy. TICKET.txt says which port it must serve on. The old `legacy` service shares this box and must not be disturbed. `systemctl` and `journalctl` here are mocks that treat the sandbox as / (use the ones in bin/).
mission.objective: Make webapp start and keep working: `systemctl is-active webapp` is active and `curl http://127.0.0.1:PORT/health` (PORT from TICKET.txt) answers 200, also after a `systemctl restart webapp`. The `legacy` unit must keep running on its own port, untouched (same process).

mission.name: Routing Puzzle: Permission Fix
mission.description: In the linux war games lab, a task related to Routing Puzzle needs cleanup before the handoff.
mission.objective: Set the mode of routing-puzzle.sh to 640

mission.name: Wedged apt
mission.description: apt and dpkg are wedged after an interrupted upgrade on web-04. Nobody can run dpkg on that box, but you have its captured package database: sysroot/var/lib/dpkg/status. FORMAT.md defines exactly what the three reports must contain.
mission.objective: From sysroot/var/lib/dpkg/status write broken.txt (every package whose state is not `installed`, with its state), unsatisfied.txt (installed packages with a version-constrained dependency that the installed version of that dependency fails) and fix_order.txt (the packages that still need configuring, dependencies first), exactly as FORMAT.md describes. Do not modify the status file.

mission.name: The Swarm
mission.description: Load average is 40 on app-03. A swarm of `crunch` processes keeps respawning whenever someone kills one, and the on-call who looked first swears that one of the members is not what it pretends to be. Three legitimate `app` processes serve customers on the same box.
mission.objective: Get rid of the whole swarm, and keep it gone: ten seconds after you finish, no swarm process may exist, and the three `app` processes must be the same PIDs as before. Then write hidden.txt: the real, absolute executable path of the swarm member that is disguised as something else (one line).

mission.name: web-02 Triage
mission.description: We think web-02 was breached. The triage collector left triage/: the auth log, shell histories, cron and systemd files, the dpkg file lists, the suspicious binary itself and stat.tsv (captured path, mtime and ctime of interesting files). HOST.txt has the server's time zone and the other facts the collector recorded.
mission.objective: Write incident.json with exactly four keys. first_malicious_login: {time_utc (ISO 8601, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`), ip} of the first login by someone who should not have had access. persistence: the sorted list of files that define the attacker's persistence (the cron.d file, the unit file and the authorized_keys file; not enable symlinks), as absolute paths on the host. exfil_host: the host name (no port) the dropped binary reports to. dropped_binary: its absolute path on the host. Do not modify anything under triage/.

mission.name: Boot Scare
mission.description: web-05 was cloned to new hardware and will not boot. `./boot-sim sysroot` walks the boot chain of the cloned root (GRUB menu, kernel and initrd, the initramfs root-device logic, fstab and the default systemd target) and stops at the first thing that fails, so each fix may reveal the next problem. blkid.txt is the capture of the new disks. The sim reads the files as they are: it does not run update-grub or update-initramfs.
mission.objective: Make `./boot-sim sysroot` finish with `Reached multi-user.target` (exit 0) by fixing the configuration under sysroot/: the GRUB menu (boot/grub/grub.cfg), /etc/fstab and the systemd configuration under etc/systemd/ may be edited; kernels, initrds and the /dev/disk tree are the hardware and must stay as they are. Pick the boot entry properly: do not remove entries or rewrite files that are not at fault.
concepts: GRUB default entry and submenu paths (1>2)

mission.name: Log Maze
mission.description: One checkout request in fifty fails with a 502 and nobody knows which of the five services starts it. gateway, checkout, payments, inventory and notifier each log in their own format and clock, and call the request ID something different. logs/ holds an hour of all five; TICKET.txt has the gateway's request ID for one failing request. TIMES.md lists each service's time format.
mission.objective: Write rootcause.txt (two lines: the service that logged the earliest ERROR on any failing request, then that ERROR line copied verbatim) and timeline.tsv for the ticket's request: one line per log event of that request, in time order, tab-separated as `UTC-time<TAB>service<TAB>level` with the time as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ (use .000 where a log has no milliseconds). A multi-line stack trace is part of the event whose line starts it. Do not modify logs/.
concepts: correlating logs by ID across formats

mission.name: Pager at 03:12
mission.description: 03:12: the shop returns 502. The service is down, the volume is full, and something keeps writing. INCIDENT.md has the page and the postmortem vocabulary; etc/shop/RETENTION.md says what may be deleted. `systemctl`, `journalctl` and `crontab` in bin/ are mocks (the sandbox is /), and cron here really runs, one simulated minute every couple of seconds.
mission.objective: Resolve the incident for good. The shop service is active and `curl http://127.0.0.1:PORT/health` (PORT in etc/shop/shop.env) answers 200 and keeps doing so; whatever was filling the disk is stopped for good in every place cron reads (the legitimate jobs stay), disk usage is under half the limit according to RETENTION.md with the evidence kept, and the leaked deploy key is gone from every config and authorized_keys file while the legitimate keys stay. Then write postmortem.json with first_bad_cron_run (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`, the first run of the runaway job), key_fingerprint (SHA256:...), deploy_id and cause_chain (root cause first, tokens from INCIDENT.md).
concepts: live processes that undo a fix
